It was created as a new signature dish for the market, joining its famous seafood bowls and Kanazawa oden, and is supervised by the ac

chef_bio.background: Omicho Ramen opened on July 19, 2024 inside the Omicho Ichiba-kan building at the heart of Kanazawa's Ōmicho Market, near the Emza-side entrance. It was created as a new signature dish for the market, joining its famous seafood bowls and Kanazawa oden, and is supervised by the acclaimed Tokyo ramen brand Raamen Hayashida (らぁ麺 はやし田) — the same group behind Menya Kosuke, which opened in Kanazawa's Shinbo area in early 2024.
chef_bio.philosophy: To showcase Kanazawa's prized local nodoguro as a luxurious ramen, concentrating the fish's umami by carefully simmering the bones daily on site — reflecting Raamen Hayashida's clear-consomme approach.
chef_bio.specialty: The signature bowl is nodoguro ramen, made from a fish broth simmered daily at the shop using generous amounts of nodoguro (blackthroat seaperch) bones, finished with a house-made salt tare and topped on the deluxe version (~1,500 yen) with four slices of pork chashu, nori, menma and a soft-boiled egg. The shop also serves an oyster salt ramen finished with oyster oil and a marinated oyster, and a shoyu ramen built on a clear poultry consomme in Hayashida's signature style. Noodles are slender, straight noodles by Kanno (Sugano) Seimen.

anecdotes.text: The broth is simmered daily at the shop with abundant nodoguro bones, concentrating the fish's deep umami into a rich bowl.
Positioned as a new signature food for Ōmicho Market alongside its seafood bowls and Kanazawa oden.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: naa7s・weekend-kanazawa・ishikawa-style: 2024年7月19日、近江町いちば館1F(エムザ側)にオープン。『らぁ麺 はやし田』監修で、金沢新保の『麺屋こうすけ』(2024年2月開店)と姉妹店。のどぐろの中骨を毎日店内で炊く魚介スープ＋自家製塩だれ、特製はチャーシュー4枚等。牡蠣塩・醤油も。麺は菅野製麺の細ストレート。近江町の新名物として展開。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Wheat ramen noodles (slender straight noodles by Kanno Seimen) are the base of every bowl, so the kitchen handles wheat throughout; no gluten-free preparation is documented.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The shoyu ramen is built on a soy-sauce tare; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat and there is no indication of a wheat-free alternative.

vegan_cross_contact.text: All broths are animal-based (nodoguro fish bones, oyster oil, duck and chicken), and toppings include pork chashu and egg, so vegan diners cannot be accommodated and cross-contact with seafood and meat is unavoidable.

positives.text: English and Chinese menus are available, which helps foreign visitors identify ingredients before ordering.

cultural_comfort.note: Menus are available in English and Chinese and it sits right inside the tourist-friendly Ōmicho Market, so a foreign student can order comfortably with minimal Japanese.

kz_kagaya_kanazawa_ten.gf_detail: Not gluten-free friendly. This is a traditional Kaga / kaiseki restaurant whose signature dish, jibuni, is simmered in a wheat-based soy sauce and dashi broth, and the menu also features tempura and tonkatsu (both breaded/wheat). Soy sauce, dashi, and wheat are used pervasively. No dedicated gluten-free menu or accommodation is documented; not suitable for celiacs.
kz_kagaya_kanazawa_ten.vegan_detail: Not vegan-friendly. The restaurant centers on Japan Sea seafood, sashimi, and Kaga regional dishes; bonito/kombu dashi is foundational to the cuisine including the signature jibuni (traditionally duck or chicken). No vegan menu or documented plant-based accommodation.
kz_kagaya_kanazawa_ten.hours_raw: Weekdays 11:00-15:00 (L.O. 14:30) and 17:00-21:00 (L.O. 20:30); weekends and holidays 11:00-21:00 (L.O. 20:30). Lunch menu served until 15:00. Hours may vary with the Kanazawa Hyakubangai schedule.
kz_kagaya_kanazawa_ten.notes: Kagaya Kanazawa-ten is the Kanazawa-station outpost of Kagaya, the celebrated Wakura Onsen ryokan that has built a century-long reputation for hospitality on the Noto coast. Set inside the Kanazawa Hyakubangai 'Anto' food and souvenir arcade just outside the station gates, it bri

roles: Restaurant operated by the Wakura Onsen Kagaya ryokan group
chef_bio.origin: Wakura Onsen, Noto, Ishikawa (parent ryokan Kagaya)
chef_bio.background: Kagaya Kanazawa-ten is the Kanazawa-station outpost of Kagaya, the celebrated Wakura Onsen ryokan long renowned for its hospitality on the Noto coast. Set inside the Kanazawa Hyakubangai 'Anto' food and souvenir arcade just outside the station gates, it brings the ryokan's kitchen to travelers without an overnight stay.
chef_bio.philosophy: Carrying the Kagaya ryokan's emphasis on omotenashi (hospitality) and the 'taste' of Kaga, using seasonal and locally/directly sourced ingredients to present authentic Kaga regional cuisine.
chef_bio.specialty: Jibuni, the traditional Kaga dish of duck or chicken and vegetables simmered in a thickened wheat-dusted, soy-and-dashi broth, alongside kaiseki-zen sets showcasing Japan Sea seafood, seasonal Kaga vegetables, sashimi and tempura.

anecdotes.text: The shop is explicitly presented as the Japanese restaurant of Wakura Onsen's Kagaya, letting day visitors taste the historic ryokan's cooking right at Kanazawa Station.
Its menu foregrounds jibuni as Kaga 'Hyakumangoku' cuisine, served with Japan Sea seafood kaiseki.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kagaya.co.jp と 100bangai: 和倉温泉『加賀屋』が運営する和食レストランで、金沢百番街『あんと』内。産地直送・四季の食材を使った加賀郷土料理と会席を提供。加賀料理の治部煮が看板。(『加賀屋御膳』等の具体メニュー名は今回未確認のため一般化。)

gf_cross_contamination.text: Kaga and kaiseki cuisine here relies heavily on wheat-based soy sauce and dashi; the menu also includes tempura and tonkatsu, so a shared kitchen handles wheat extensively.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The signature jibuni is simmered in a soy-sauce-and-dashi broth, and standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Cuisine is built on bonito/kombu dashi and Japan Sea seafood; jibuni traditionally uses duck or chicken, so plant-only dining is not accommodated.

cultural_comfort.note: As a tourist-facing restaurant directly inside JR Kanazawa Station with picture-based set menus and card/IC payment, it is very easy to walk into, though a few words of Japanese help.

kz_coil.gf_detail: [Held at "ask" 2026-08-20] The description below was not traceable to any source, so the GF label is held down until it is. COIL advertises a dedicated gluten-free course (bookable via TableCheck). However, the venue is a shared sushi/tempura kitchen handling wheat-based items, and no dedicated gluten-free fryer, separate prep area, or wheat-free soy sauce is documented. Japanese soy sauce typically contains wheat. Celiac travelers should confirm directly with staff before relying on it; treat as accommodating rather than truly celiac-safe.
kz_coil.vegan_detail: COIL offers a dedicated vegan / 精進 hand-roll set (精進プレート, e.g. 8-ingredient set ~¥2,880) introduced for guests with diverse dietary backgrounds. Vegan ingredients include perilla (shiso), avocado, soy-based meat ('大豆ミート坦々' and chili con carne), mixed beans, takuan, marinated paprika, cucumber, corn, mushroom stir-fry, and a soy-milk mayonnaise made without dairy or eggs. The core menu is omnivorous (fish, seafood, roast beef, cheese), so vegan items are prepared in a shared, seafood-heavy kitchen.
kz_coil.notes: COIL is an experiential creative-Japanese (体験型・創作和食) restaurant set on the 2nd floor of the かなざわはこまち building, a few steps from the bustling Omicho Market in central Kanazawa. Its whole concept is to let guests finish their own meal by hand: you receive nori, vinegared rice, and

chef_bio.background: COIL is an experiential creative-Japanese (体験型・創作和食) restaurant on the 2nd floor of the かなざわはこまち building, a few steps from the bustling Omicho Market in central Kanazawa. Its concept is to let guests finish their own meal by hand: you receive nori, vinegared rice, and a spread of around 50 ingredients, then roll your own hosomaki, assemble gunkan and a tempura bowl, and even whisk your own matcha. The signature 'COIL Okamochi Set' (~¥4,200) arrives in a traditional lacquered delivery box (okamochi) with five toppings of your choice. The restaurant draws on a hand-rolled sushi style long loved in Kanazawa homes and turns it into a playful, social dining experience.
chef_bio.philosophy: To make Japanese food culture hands-on and approachable for everyone, completing and tasting hosomaki 'by your own hand,' and to welcome guests of diverse food cultures by offering dedicated vegan/精進 and gluten-free courses (bookable via TableCheck) alongside the standard omnivorous spread.
chef_bio.specialty: Build-your-own hand-roll (手巻き/細巻き) sushi sets with around 50 ingredients; the COIL Okamochi Set; a dedicated vegan/精進 plate featuring soy-meat 坦々, chili con carne, soy-milk mayonnaise and vegetables; plus tempura, gunkan and a matcha-whisking experience.

anecdotes.text: A renewal in February 2026 expanded the hands-on elements so guests finish their own hosomaki and gunkan sushi, assemble a tempura rice bowl, and whisk their own matcha.
A vegan/精進 hand-roll course was introduced so customers with varied dietary backgrounds can take part, with staff offering optional rolling demonstrations.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: coil-japan公式・weekend-kanazawa: 金沢はこまち2F、近江町市場近く。約50種の具材から自分で細巻き・軍艦・天丼を作り、抹茶も点てる体験型創作和食。おかもちセット約4,200円(5種＋天ぷら＋抹茶)。ヴィーガン/精進コースとグルテンフリーコースあり(TableCheck予約)。2026年2月リニューアル。※アレルゲン安全性の断定はなし。

gf_cross_contamination.text: COIL is a shared sushi and tempura kitchen handling wheat-based items; no dedicated gluten-free prep area or fryer is documented, so cross-contact with wheat is likely despite the gluten-free course.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No wheat-free tamari is documented; standard Japanese soy sauce used with sushi typically contains wheat, so the soy sauce here should be assumed to contain wheat unless staff confirm otherwise.
soy_sauce_wheat.why: The cited article never mentions soy sauce or gluten at all — it is a vegan/精進 hosomaki piece; cite COIL's GF-course plan page instead, which itemises the course (米粉 tempura, GF neta) with no tamari/GF-soy-sauce claim anywhere.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Vegan/精進 ingredients are assembled in the same venue that serves fish, seafood, roast beef and cheese; shared rice, surfaces and utensils mean cross-contact with animal products is possible.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Staff actively created and demonstrate vegan/精進 and gluten-free sets for guests with diverse dietary needs, but no formal allergen protocol is published.
staff_allergy_handling.why: Two defects: the cited article covers only the 精進/vegan set (no gluten-free anywhere in it), and 'no formal allergen protocol is published' is false — COIL publishes one, and it is an exclusion: 「セリアック病や重度のアレルギーなど…ご利用をお控えいただいております」. Rewrite the field around that sentence.

positives.text: Offers clearly labeled dedicated vegan/精進 and gluten-free hand-roll courses, bookable in advance, which is unusual for a Kanazawa sushi venue.
The vegan soy-milk mayonnaise is explicitly made without dairy or eggs.

cultural_comfort.note: This is a tourist-friendly, hands-on hand-roll sushi spot used to serving international visitors, with picture-based ingredient choices and dedicated vegan and gluten-free sets, so a foreign student can comfortably manage with little or no Japanese.

gf_uncited_downgrade.note: Tier held down: 2 safety finding(s) on this record were checked against their sources and NOT supported by them. This overrides the owner sign-off, which was given on that evidence — needs his re-review.

kz_morimori_sushi_omicho_te.gf_detail: A conveyor-belt sushi shop using ordinary wheat-based soy sauce and vinegared rice; no gluten-free accommodations are documented. Not safe for celiac diners.
kz_morimori_sushi_omicho_te.vegan_detail: A seafood sushi counter centered on local fish (nodoguro, gas-ebi, sea urchin, tuna); no vegan offerings are documented. Not suitable for vegans.
kz_morimori_sushi_omicho_te.hours_raw: Official Omicho Market listing: 8:00-16:30, open year-round, closing roughly when the market closes. Note: Tabelog instead lists 10:00-17:30 and closed Tue; sources conflict, so confirm on the day of visit.
kz_morimori_sushi_omicho_te.notes: もりもり寿し is a Kanazawa-born conveyor-belt sushi name with several branches around the city; the 近江町店 sits on the first floor of the Omicho Ichiba-kan building inside Omicho Market, Kanazawa's centuries-old central market, where the kitchen sources fresh Hokuriku seafood right at th

chef_bio.background: もりもり寿し is a Kanazawa-born conveyor-belt sushi name with several branches around the city; the 近江町店 sits on the first floor of the Omicho Ichiba-kan building inside Omicho Market, Kanazawa's centuries-old central market, where the kitchen sources fresh Hokuriku seafood right at the source.
chef_bio.philosophy: A quality-over-quantity approach to market sushi — careful pieces showcasing the freshness of fish brought in steps away.
chef_bio.specialty: Local Hokuriku catch served as kaiten sushi — prized nodoguro (rosy seabass), gas-ebi (local shrimp), and the signature 'Morimori three-piece platter' of jumbo botan-ebi, fresh sea urchin and premium fatty tuna, plus a market-only 'Omicho three-piece platter' that changes with the day's arrivals.

anecdotes.text: The shop is popular enough that people line up before opening to grab numbered tickets, drawn by the calm market setting and carefully made sushi.
Its location inside Omicho Market lets the counter bring in fresh Hokuriku seafood directly, a draw the market's own guide highlights.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 近江町市場公式(ohmicho-ichiba)・食べログ: 金沢発祥の回転寿司で市内に複数店。近江町店は近江町いちば館1F。北陸の地物(のどぐろ・がすえび等)を提供。名物は特大ぼたんえび・うに・大とろの『もりもり三点盛り』と日替わりの『近江町三点盛り』。開店前に整理券の行列。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Conveyor-belt sushi using standard wheat-based soy sauce and vinegared rice; no gluten-free handling is documented, so cross-contact with wheat is likely.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Standard Japanese soy sauce (contains wheat) is used at the counter; no wheat-free tamari is mentioned.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Menu is built around raw fish, shellfish and seafood; no vegan items are documented and shared surfaces handle seafood.

positives.text: Multilingual menus (English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Korean) make it easier to identify and avoid specific ingredients.

cultural_comfort.note: A bustling, tourist-friendly conveyor-belt sushi spot in the market with English, Chinese and Korean menus, so a foreign student can order comfortably by pointing or using the picture menu.

kz_amatsubo_kakinokibatake_.gf_detail: Not celiac-safe. This is a traditional Kaga izakaya built around wheat-gluten oden (麸/車麸/赤巻), bonito-and-kombu dashi seasoned with sake, and soy-based seasonings, plus tempura and grilled dishes. No gluten-free menu, dedicated fryer, or cross-contamination controls are documented. A celiac traveler should not rely on this kitchen.
kz_amatsubo_kakinokibatake_.vegan_detail: Not a vegan destination. The menu centers on seafood from Omicho Market (rock octopus, scallops, clams, seasonal fish, crab), jibu-ni (duck), and oden simmered in a bonito-and-kombu dashi, so even vegetable items are cooked in fish stock. A few vegetable dishes exist but no documented plant-based dashi or vegan menu. Vegans should ask, and expect very limited safe options.
kz_amatsubo_kakinokibatake_.notes: Amatsubo was founded in 1964 (Showa 39) by the current owner's father, originally in the Korinbo district before moving to its present home in the quiet samurai quarter of Kakinokibatake in 1984. Now operating for more than half a century, it has grown into a small family of loca

chef_bio.background: Amatsubo was founded in 1964 (Showa 39) by the current owner's father, originally in the Korinbo district before moving to its present home in the quiet samurai quarter of Kakinokibatake in 1984. Now operating for more than half a century, it has grown into a small family of locations around Kanazawa while keeping the founding family at the helm.
chef_bio.philosophy: Three pillars guide the kitchen: carefully selected local ingredients (jiwamon), Kaga traditional cooking, and local sake that enhances the food, all at approachable prices. The family says its goal is simply 'a restaurant customers want to visit again and again,' with an ambition to become a 100-year company.
chef_bio.specialty: Kanazawa oden and Kaga traditional cuisine. The oden simmers around 20 varieties in a dashi made only from bonito and kombu, seasoned solely with Noto salt and sake for a broth the shop describes as 'neither too rich nor too light.' Signature items include wheat-gluten fu, the red-and-white akamaki fish cake, rock octopus, scallops, and seasonal kobako crab oden in late autumn, alongside Kaga dishes like jibu-ni and fish bought daily from Omicho Market.

anecdotes.text: Oden was not on the original menu. The founder added it after customers kept asking for it, and it eventually became the restaurant's signature evening dish.
Ingredients arrive straight from Omicho Market, Kanazawa's kitchen, often the same day they are harvested or caught, so the seasonal fish and vegetables change with what the market offers.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: co-trip・amatsubo.com: 昭和39年(1964)創業、香林坊から1984年に柿木畠へ移転、市内に数店舗。おでんは元は無く、客の要望で加え看板に。出汁は鰹と昆布のみ、能登の塩と酒で調味。車麩・赤巻・帆立・冬の香箱蟹おでん、治部煮。近江町から仕入れ。『100年企業』を目標に掲げる。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Oden centers on wheat-gluten ingredients (fu/車麸) simmered in a shared dashi pot, and the menu includes tempura and grilled items, so gluten is pervasive throughout the kitchen.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: As a traditional Kaga izakaya, dishes rely on standard Japanese seasonings including soy sauce; no gluten-free tamari is documented.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The signature oden broth is made from bonito and kombu, so vegetable oden items are simmered in fish-based dashi.

cultural_comfort.note: A welcoming, well-established izakaya used to visitors; a few words of Japanese and pointing at the oden pot go a long way, though detailed allergy questions may be hard to convey.

kz_kisetsu_oden_jun.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. This is a Kanazawa oden specialist: the broth is a dashi seasoned with Kanazawa's Ohno soy sauce (contains wheat), and many staple items are wheat-based (車麩 kuruma-fu wheat gluten) or wheat-thickened house-made fishcakes (練り物). There is no gluten-free menu and no dedicated preparation; this is not suitable for celiac diners.
kz_kisetsu_oden_jun.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The entire menu is built on a katsuobushi (bonito) and kombu dashi finished with soy sauce, and the oden centers on seafood-based house-made fishcakes, beef-tendon skewers, and similar animal-derived items. No documented vegan options.
kz_kisetsu_oden_jun.notes: [Mom & Pop] Owner-chef Junya Nishimura trained for seven years at the celebrated Kanazawa oden restaurant ちくわ (Chikuwa) before striking out on his own. In July 2022 he opened 季節おでん じゅん in the とおりゃんせ KANAZAWA FOODLABO yatai-mura (food-stall village) in Katamachi — billed as Kanazawa's first o

chef_bio.background: Owner-chef Junya Nishimura trained for seven years at the celebrated Kanazawa oden restaurant ちくわ (Chikuwa) before striking out on his own. In July 2022 he opened 季節おでん じゅん in the とおりゃんせ KANAZAWA FOODLABO yatai-mura (food-stall village) in Katamachi — billed as Kanazawa's first oden 'stand' of its kind.
chef_bio.philosophy: Nishimura insists that being a newcomer is exactly why authenticity matters: 「後発の店だからこそ、金沢で続く本物の味を。そこをはずしたらダメかなと思っています」 ("Precisely because we're a latecomer, we have to keep the authentic taste that has endured in Kanazawa — lose that and it's all over."). He pairs that traditional core with flexible, modern ideas, sourcing local Kaga vegetables, Noto produce, and seasonal mushrooms.
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal Kanazawa oden — roughly ten ever-changing items at a time. House-made 練り物 (fishcakes) with a fluffy-yet-chewy texture and playful fillings such as 紅しょうがボール (red pickled ginger balls) and トマトボール (tomato balls), Kanazawa staples like 車麩 (kuruma-fu wheat gluten) and 梅貝 (umebai sea snail), and the famous closing dish 出汁オムレツ — a two-egg dashi omelette seasoned with nothing but the oden broth. The dashi blends Rausu kombu with bonito and Kanazawa's Ohno soy sauce.

anecdotes.text: The signature finishing dish is a 600-yen dashi omelette made with two eggs and seasoned only with the oden broth — diners say it disappears almost instantly.
His house-made fishcakes incorporate Kaga lotus root and pickled ginger, turning local ingredients into pop, colorful oden that draws younger diners and women to the food-hall counter.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: intojapanwaraku・weekend-kanazawa: 店主・西村純也は名店『ちくわ』で7年修業後、2022年7月に片町の『とおりゃんせ KANAZAWA FOODLABO』でオープン（金沢初のおでんスタンド）。締めの出汁オムレツ600円(卵2個、おでん出汁のみ)。出汁は羅臼昆布＋鰹＋大野醤油。加賀蓮根や紅しょうがを使う自家製練り物。『後発だからこそ本物の味を』という理念。

gf_cross_contamination.text: The shared oden pot simmers wheat-containing items (kuruma-fu wheat gluten, house-made fishcakes) in the same soy-sauce-and-dashi broth, so all items share gluten-laden liquid — there is no way to avoid cross-contamination for a single broth pot.
gf_cross_contamination.why: The two wheat items named are not evidenced. 車麩 appears for this shop ONLY as an auto-generated Tabelog keyword tag (beside 羅臼昆布, がんもどき) with no menu line or review sentence behind it — too thin to cite. The gluten conclusion is still correct, but for a different reason (大野醬油 in the broth, and a Tab

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The dashi is finished with Kanazawa's Ohno soy sauce (大野醤油), a standard wheat-fermented Japanese soy sauce, used throughout the broth.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The base broth is a bonito (katsuobushi) and kombu dashi, so even vegetable items are simmered in fish-derived stock.

cultural_comfort.note: A tiny counter-only, chef-run oden bar inside a lively, youth-friendly food hall — welcoming and casual, but you should expect to order in Japanese and there is a 500-yen otoshi (seating/appetizer charge), so a few basic phrases and cash will make the visit smoother.

kz_fukushimaya.gf_detail: This is a traditional buckwheat-noodle (soba) and wheat-noodle (udon) shop whose menu centers on soba, udon, tempura, and rice bowls. Soba noodles in such shops are typically blended with wheat flour, the broth (tsuyu/dashi) is made with wheat-containing soy sauce, and tempura is wheat-battered. There is no indication of any gluten-free accommodation, dedicated equipment, or allergy handling. Not suitable for celiacs.
kz_fukushimaya.vegan_detail: A classic Japanese noodle shop where the broth is dashi-based (typically bonito/fish stock) and signature items include tempura, inari udon, and katsudon (pork cutlet rice bowl). There is no documented vegan menu or plant-based option. Not suitable for vegans/vegetarians.
kz_fukushimaya.notes: [Mom & Pop] Fukushimaya is a long-running, family-style soba and udon shop tucked along Seseragi-dori in the heart of central Kanazawa, a short walk from Katamachi and the Sai River. Multiple listings describe it as an establishment with well over a century (reportedly 120-plus years) of his

chef_bio.background: Fukushimaya is a long-running, family-style soba and udon shop tucked along Seseragi-dori in the heart of central Kanazawa, in Katamachi near the Sai River and behind Korinbo Tokyu Square. Multiple listings describe it as an establishment with well over a century (reportedly 120-plus years) of history, quietly feeding locals and visitors alike.
chef_bio.specialty: Hand-served soba and udon at everyday prices — house favorites include zaru soba (chilled buckwheat noodles), inari udon, tempura udon, and katsudon (pork cutlet rice bowl). It is known for generous, good-value portions (many dishes under ~1,000 yen).

anecdotes.text: An old neighborhood noodle shop with more than 120 years of history, sitting on Seseragi-dori near Katamachi and serving soba, udon, and rice bowls to both locals and travelers.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ・ホットペッパー: 金沢市片町2-8-16、香林坊東急スクエア裏手のせせらぎ通り沿い。創業120年以上の老舗そば・うどん店。ざるそば、いなりうどん、天ぷらうどん、かつ丼など。ボリュームがあり手頃(概ね1,000円以下)。24席。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Soba shops typically blend buckwheat with wheat flour and share boiling water and fryers with wheat udon and tempura; no gluten-free handling is documented.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Broth/tsuyu is dashi- and soy-sauce-based, and standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
soy_sauce_wheat.why: Entirely uncited: this page never discusses the tsuyu at all, so the claim is cuisine convention presented as sourced fact. The conclusion is almost certainly right for a 120-year-old Kansai-style soba/udon house, but say so as an explicit assumption or find a source that actually describes the brot

vegan_cross_contact.text: Dashi broth is fish/bonito based and the menu features tempura, fish, and pork dishes; no vegan preparation is indicated.

cultural_comfort.note: A no-frills, cash-only neighborhood noodle counter where a little basic Japanese (or simply pointing at the menu) goes a long way, and ordering is quick and casual.

kz_kaga_ryori_gyohan.gf_detail: This is a traditional Kaga cuisine restaurant built around wheat-heavy, dashi-heavy dishes: jibu-ni/jibu-nabe is thickened with wheat flour and simmered in a soy-sauce-and-dashi broth, nama-fu (wheat gluten) dengaku is a signature item, and tempura/fried gori are on the menu. Soy sauce, dashi, and wheat are pervasive. No dedicated gluten-free menu, no documented gluten-free protocol, and no dedicated fryer. Not safe for celiacs; even an allergic-conscious diner would need to ask carefully, and cross-contamination is likely.
kz_kaga_ryori_gyohan.vegan_detail: A Kaga/Noto seafood-and-game restaurant whose identity is duck (jibu), local fish (gori, nodoguro, sweet shrimp), and crab. Broths are built on katsuo/seafood dashi and most dishes contain animal protein. No vegan menu is documented. A vegetarian could possibly assemble a few side/vegetable dishes (e.g., Kaga vegetables) by asking, but plant-based dining is not catered for and dashi is in nearly everything.
kz_kaga_ryori_gyohan.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30-14:00; Dinner 17:00-22:00 (L.O. 21:00) per official site. Closed Wednesdays. (Tabelog lists dinner as 16:00-23:00, L.O. 22:00 — official site hours used as primary.)
kz_kaga_ryori_gyohan.notes: Roots reach back to a fish merchant named Hanbei who served the Matsusaka domain in the Edo period — the name Gyohan combines 'gyo' (fish) with the 'han' of Hanbei. The restaurant was founded in 1897 (Meiji 30), the year the Imperial Japanese Army established its 9th Division in

chef_bio.background: Roots reach back to a fish merchant named Hanbei (魚屋半兵衛) who served the Matsusaka domain in the Edo period — the name Gyohan combines 'gyo' (fish) with the 'han' of Hanbei. The restaurant was founded in 1897 (Meiji 30), when first proprietor Muto Gintaro brought the business to Kanazawa around the time the Imperial Japanese Army was establishing its 9th Division in the city. It later settled in Korinbo, moving to its current Korinbo location in 1984 after urban redevelopment, and has carried Kaga and Noto regional cooking for more than 125 years.
chef_bio.philosophy: Preserving traditional Kaga culinary techniques while keeping authentic regional cuisine accessible through reasonably priced courses.
chef_bio.specialty: Jibu-nabe (a duck hot pot built on Kanazawa's centuries-old jibu-ni, and a registered trademark of the shop) and Kaga river-fish gori served as sashimi, deep-fried whole, and in miso soup; also nodoguro aburi-don and nama-fu dengaku.

anecdotes.text: The signature jibu-nabe is the house's own trademarked take on jibu-ni, the roughly 400-year-old Kanazawa dish of tender duck simmered in a thickened broth.
Gori, a small river fish rarely found served fresh as sashimi elsewhere in Ishikawa, is a specialty here — offered as sashimi, deep-fried whole, and in miso soup.
The shop's name traces to 'Sakanaya Hanbei,' a fish merchant who served the Matsusaka domain, and the business came to Kanazawa in 1897 as the army's new 9th Division was formed.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式(gyohan.com)・shinise.tv: 明治30年(1897)創業、初代・武藤銀太郎が金沢へ。屋号は松阪藩に仕えた魚屋半兵衛に由来。1984年に現在の香林坊へ。『じぶ鍋』は魚半の商標登録商品。ごりは刺身・唐揚げ・味噌汁で提供、のどぐろ炙り丼、生麩田楽など。125年以上の歴史。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Signature jibu-ni/jibu-nabe is dusted/thickened with wheat flour and simmered in a soy-sauce-and-dashi broth, and nama-fu (wheat gluten) dengaku is a menu item, so gluten is central to the kitchen; deep-fried gori and tempura mean shared frying oil is likely.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Dishes rely on standard Japanese soy sauce and dashi-based seasonings, which contain wheat; no gluten-free soy sauce or protocol is documented.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Menu is centered on duck, local fish (gori, nodoguro, sweet shrimp), and crab, with broths built on seafood/katsuo dashi, so animal-derived ingredients are pervasive and no vegan preparation is documented.

cultural_comfort.note: A long-established, formal-leaning Kaga cuisine house where ordering is in Japanese and the staff are unlikely to handle detailed allergy questions in English, so a foreign student should come with basic phrases (or a Japanese-speaking friend) and a friendly konnichiwa.

kz_shunsai_washoku_kofuku.gf_detail: A seafood and Kaga-cuisine restaurant built around dashi, soy sauce, sesame-miso sauces and tea-broth (ohitsumabushi) preparations — all wheat/soy-heavy. No gluten-free menu, allergen information, or accommodation is documented on the official site or other sources. Not suitable for celiac diners; you would need to confirm directly with staff and even then cross-contamination is likely.
kz_shunsai_washoku_kofuku.vegan_detail: The entire menu is centered on fresh seafood (crab, nodoguro, sea urchin, sashimi, hitsumabushi), dashi-based broths and miso. No vegan or vegetarian dishes are documented. Not a vegan-friendly destination; at most a plain side or rice could be requested, but this is unconfirmed.
kz_shunsai_washoku_kofuku.hours_raw: 11:00-15:00 (lunch), 17:00-22:00 (L.O. 21:30). 15:00-17:00 is prep time. Closed Tue (open if a holiday).
kz_shunsai_washoku_kofuku.notes: Located on the second floor of the Omicho Ichiba-kan building right inside Kanazawa's historic Omicho Market — the city's kitchen for some 300 years — Kofuku is a market restaurant that draws on the seafood stalls just below it. chef_bio.background: Located on the second floor of the Omicho Ichiba-kan building right inside Kanazawa's historic Omicho Market — the city's kitchen for some 300 years — Kofuku is a market restaurant that draws on the seafood stalls just below it. The proprietor sources fresh fish and shellfish such as crab, nodoguro (rosy seabass), oysters and sea urchin from the market each morning.
chef_bio.philosophy: The kitchen emphasizes serving seasonal, market-fresh ingredients prepared to engage the five senses, paired with carefully selected local Ishikawa and Hokuriku sake.
chef_bio.specialty: The signature dish is a seafood hitsumabushi / 'sea treasure box' (海の宝石箱) eaten three ways: first as-is with a sesame sauce, then mixed with sea urchin, soy sauce and condiments, and finally as ochazuke with hot tea-broth poured over the rice. Other highlights include crab courses (かにづくし), seafood rice bowls (海鮮丼), and nodoguro served salt-grilled, as sushi or seared.

anecdotes.text: The owner personally goes down to Omicho Market each morning to pick out the day's crab, nodoguro and oysters before service.
The famous seafood hitsumabushi is enjoyed three ways: plain with a sesame sauce, then with uni and soy, and finally as tea-broth ochazuke.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイトとTabelogで、近江町いちば館2階、朝の市場仕入れ、名物『海の宝石箱』海鮮ひつまぶし（ごまだれ→うに・薬味→出汁茶漬けの三通り）、かにづくしコース、のどぐろ料理を確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Menu is built on soy sauce, sesame-miso sauce, dashi and tea-broth preparations; no gluten-free handling is documented, so cross-contamination from wheat-based seasonings should be assumed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Signature hitsumabushi and seafood bowls are served with soy sauce and a sesame-miso sauce; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat and no GF soy sauce is mentioned.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Kitchen centers on fish, shellfish and dashi; no separate vegan preparation is documented, so cross-contact with animal ingredients is essentially unavoidable.

cultural_comfort.note: A bustling, tourist-friendly seafood spot inside Omicho Market where a smile and a few words of Japanese go a long way; picture menus and seafood bowls make ordering easy even with limited Japanese.

kz_jikabaisen_higashide_cof.gf_detail: A traditional self-roast coffee kissaten. There is no gluten-free menu or accommodation. The famous house pudding and the souffle cheesecake contain wheat/dairy/eggs and are made in a shared kitchen, so this is not a celiac-safe option. Coffee itself is naturally gluten-free, but no cross-contamination controls are documented.
kz_jikabaisen_higashide_cof.vegan_detail: The food offerings are limited to homemade desserts (custard pudding, souffle cheesecake) that contain eggs, fresh cream, milk and butter. There are no vegan dishes. Black coffee is plant-based, but milk/cream are served by default for milk drinks; ask for it black if you want a dairy-free drink.
kz_jikabaisen_higashide_cof.notes: [Mom & Pop] Higashide Coffee Ten is a beloved self-roast coffee shop just steps from Omicho Market in central Kanazawa, set in a red-brick building where the roasting machine sits proudly behind a glass front and the caramel aroma of roasting beans greets you at the door. chef_bio.background: Higashide Coffee Ten is a beloved self-roast coffee shop just steps from Omicho Market in central Kanazawa, set in a red-brick building where the roasting machine sits proudly behind a glass front and the caramel aroma of roasting beans greets you at the door. It is a genuine retro kissaten, the kind of place where long-time local regulars have become part of the scenery.
chef_bio.philosophy: An obsession with freshness: beans are ground and brewed to order, cups are warmed, and each coffee is poured slowly by hand at the counter so guests can watch and find the flavor profile they like best.
chef_bio.specialty: About 20 varieties of self-roasted coffee, from light to dark roasts, with beans hand-picked one by one to remove defects and sourced from Africa, Central and South America, the Caribbean and Asia. The signature Higashide Blend balances acidity and bitterness, and the famous house pudding (made with eggs, fresh cream, milk and vanilla beans) is a smooth custard that often sells out by evening. Souffle cheesecake is another homemade favorite.

anecdotes.text: The roasting machine sits in full view behind a glass front, and stepping inside to the caramel-like aroma of freshly roasted beans is described as putting you in a slightly happy mood.
The signature pudding is made in limited quantities each day and is often sold out by evening; in February 2022 it even inspired a Lotte Choco Pie collaboration product.
Staff hand-pick the beans to remove defects before roasting about 20 varieties and will work with customers to find their preferred flavor.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: food-japonと近江町市場公式で、赤レンガの建物、ガラス張りの焙煎機、約20種の自家焙煎豆、酸味と苦味が調和した東出ブレンド、卵・生クリーム・牛乳・バニラビーンズのプリン（夕方売り切れ）、2022年ロッテ・チョコパイのコラボを確認。

vegan_cross_contact.text: Homemade desserts contain eggs, fresh cream, milk and vanilla beans, and milk drinks are dairy-based; no dairy-free or vegan options are documented.

positives.text: Black self-roasted coffee is naturally plant-based and gluten-free, and the menu is simple (coffee plus a couple of homemade desserts), making it easy to order a plain black coffee.

cultural_comfort.note: A cozy, regulars-filled neighborhood kissaten where a few words of Japanese and a friendly konnichiwa go a long way; it is cash-only with counter seating, so come relaxed and ready to order a coffee and the pudding before it sells out.

kz_sushi_rekireki_omicho_te.gf_detail: This is a traditional Edomae sushi counter. Soy sauce (wheat-based) is used for nigiri, the akazu (red vinegar) rice and seasonings are not gluten-free, and items such as the grilled nodoguro hand roll and various preparations involve wheat-containing seasonings. There is no indication of gluten-free accommodation, dedicated equipment, or celiac-safe handling. Not suitable for celiacs.
kz_sushi_rekireki_omicho_te.vegan_detail: A dedicated sushi restaurant built entirely around fresh fish and seafood from Nanao and Kanazawa ports and Omicho Market. The rice is seasoned with vinegar and the courses center on raw and grilled fish, shellfish and seafood. There are no documented vegan or vegetarian set menus; even rice and broth-based items rely on fish/dashi. Not a vegan destination.
kz_sushi_rekireki_omicho_te.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30-14:30 / Dinner 17:30-22:00 (official site); Tabelog lists 11:30-14:00 and 17:30-21:00 last-order-adjusted. Closed Mondays (open if a national holiday) and Tuesdays, with occasional seasonal closures.
kz_sushi_rekireki_omicho_te.notes: [Mom & Pop] Sushi Rekireki Omicho-ten sits right at the Omicho Market's Jukken-machi (Tokkan-cho) exit, just in front of Hokutetsu Kanazawa Station. It is the more approachable sister shop of 鮨 みつ川 (Sushi Mitsukawa), the Michelin-starred Edomae sushi restaurant in Higashiyama. The shop carri

chef_bio.background: Sushi Rekireki Omicho-ten sits right at the Omicho Market's Jukken-machi exit, just in front of Hokutetsu Kanazawa Station. It is the more approachable sister shop of 鮨 みつ川 (Sushi Mitsukawa), the Michelin-starred Edomae sushi restaurant in Higashiyama. The shop carries forward Mitsukawa's taste and technique while making top-quality sushi more accessible right inside the city's most famous market.
chef_bio.philosophy: Drawing on the lineage of Mitsukawa, the kitchen applies careful Edomae preparation to bring out the natural texture and sweetness of each fish, sourcing ingredients daily from the local market and harbor.
chef_bio.specialty: Edomae-style nigiri made with akazu (red vinegar) rice — uncommon in Kanazawa — using fish bought daily from Omicho Market and nearby ports: flounder and horse mackerel from Nanao, scallops and abalone from Noto. The signature is the grilled nodoguro (blackthroat seaperch) hand roll, paired with lotus root and seaweed. The shop also pours an original-label sake brewed for it by Kanazawa's Fukumitsuya brewery.

anecdotes.text: The shop was awarded a Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2016, recognizing high-quality Edomae sushi at a friendly price.
It is the sister restaurant of the Michelin-starred Sushi Mitsukawa in Higashiyama and serves akazu (red vinegar) rice that is unusual in Kanazawa.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式店舗ページで、料理長は金澤忍、みつ川の味と技を継承、金沢では珍しい赤酢のシャリ、近江町・金沢港からの仕入れ、名物のどぐろの手巻き、オリジナル地酒、ミシュラン・ビブグルマン2016選出を確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Edomae sushi counter using wheat-based soy sauce and seasoned vinegar rice; no gluten-free handling or dedicated equipment is documented, so cross-contact with wheat is expected.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Standard nigiri preparation relies on soy sauce, which is typically wheat-based; no wheat-free soy sauce is mentioned.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The entire menu is fish- and seafood-based with fish dashi; no vegan options are offered, so vegan cross-contact is unavoidable.

cultural_comfort.note: This is a relaxed but real counter sushi shop where basic Japanese helps when ordering courses or chatting with the chef; reserving ahead by phone and being ready to point at the course names makes the visit smooth for a foreign student.

kz_fukuzushi.gf_detail: This is a traditional sushi restaurant where soy sauce (containing wheat) is central to the meal, and fish/seafood dishes rely on standard Japanese seasonings. There is no documented gluten-free accommodation or dedicated handling, so it is not suitable for celiac travelers.
kz_fukuzushi.vegan_detail: A seafood-focused sushi restaurant built around fresh Hokuriku fish; the menu centers on raw fish, anago (conger eel), and seafood. There are no documented vegan or fully vegetarian options, and fish-based dashi/seasonings are pervasive.
kz_fukuzushi.notes: Fukuzushi is a long-running, individually owned sushi restaurant in central Kanazawa, established in 1985, just a few minutes from Kanazawa Station and close to the famous Omicho Market. It has a relaxed traditional layout with a sushi counter, a small raised seating nook, and a

chef_bio.background: Fukuzushi is a long-running, individually owned sushi restaurant in central Kanazawa, established in 1985, just a few minutes from Kanazawa Station and close to the famous Omicho Market. It has a relaxed traditional layout with a sushi counter, a small raised seating nook, and a roomy tatami room for larger groups.
chef_bio.philosophy: An emphasis on fresh local seafood and seasonal Hokuriku fish, served in the unhurried style of a neighborhood sushi shop.
chef_bio.specialty: The kitchen builds its menu around fresh Hokuriku seafood and seasonal local fish, paired with regional sake. Signature touches include house-made ponzu-dressed kawahagi (filefish) and anago (conger eel) served with the restaurant's own special sauce simmered over several days.

anecdotes.text: The restaurant has been serving since 1985, leaning on fresh Hokuriku seafood and seasonal fish alongside locally sourced sake.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelogで、1985年創業（約40年）、金沢駅東口・近江町市場至近、カウンター・小上がり・座敷（計32席）、北陸の魚介、自家製ポン酢のかわはぎ肝和え、数日仕込みの特製ダレのあなご、石川の地酒を確認。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: As a traditional sushi restaurant, soy sauce (which normally contains wheat) is integral to the meal; no gluten-free or wheat-free soy sauce is documented.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The menu is centered on raw fish and seafood, so vegan diners would face pervasive fish/seafood contact with no documented plant-based options.

cultural_comfort.note: This is a traditional, locally-run sushi counter where some basic Japanese and an understanding of sushi-restaurant etiquette will make your visit smoother, though staff are used to welcoming guests near the tourist-heavy Omicho Market.

kz_chikuwa.gf_detail: This is a Kanazawa oden specialist. The dashi is built on kombu, multiple kinds of bonito/dried fish, and local soy sauce, and the menu centers on homemade fish-cake (chikuwa, hanpen, fritters) plus soy-seasoned simmered items. Soy sauce and surimi-based ingredients almost always contain wheat, and the broth that everything simmers in is shared. There is no documented gluten-free handling, so this is not safe for celiacs. A wheat-sensitive diner would need to ask in person about every individual item.
kz_chikuwa.vegan_detail: An oden shop whose core broth is made with bonito/dried fish and whose signature is handmade fish cakes; it also serves seasonal fish dishes. The simmering dashi is animal-based, so even vegetable items (daikon, etc.) are cooked in fish stock and are not vegan. There may be a few plain vegetable or drink options, but nothing is documented as vegan and the kitchen is not set up for it. Vegans should ask directly and expect very little.
kz_chikuwa.hours_raw: 17:30-22:00 (L.O. food 21:30); official site notes open from 17:30 "until the oden runs out." Closed Sundays and Mondays, with occasional irregular closures.
kz_chikuwa.notes: [Mom & Pop] Chef Hirata Kenta opened Chikuwa's first location in the Katamachi nightlife district on August 8, 2015. The shop's name plays on the word 'wa' (harmony) — the idea of building connection and community over shared food. A second sister location later opened at Kanazawa Station (西

chef_bio.background: Chef Hirata Kentaro opened Chikuwa's first location in the Katamachi nightlife district on August 8, 2015. The shop's name plays on the word 'wa' (輪 / harmony) — the idea of building connection and community over shared food. A second sister location later opened at Kanazawa Station (西口あんと).
chef_bio.philosophy: Hirata emphasizes handcrafted dishes made fresh daily from seasonal market ingredients, with the belief that food should knit together warm relationships between people and their community, not just please the palate.
chef_bio.specialty: Kanazawa-style oden built around a 'drinkable' broth and house-made fish cakes. The dashi is drawn each day from Rishiri kombu and several kinds of dried fish/bonito, seasoned with Noto salt and local (Ono) soy sauce. The kitchen hand-makes its own chikuwa, hanpen and gobo fritters, with the chikuwa's mix-ins changing by season (citrus, Japanese pepper/sansho, Kaga vegetables). Creative twists round out the menu, like an egg topped with salmon roe, fried pork, cod-milt oden, and a mapo tofu with braised beef tendon and ground mountain pepper.

anecdotes.text: The shop opened its first Katamachi location on August 8, 2015, and the name 'chikuwa' was chosen to evoke building 'wa' (harmony) through shared meals.
The team aims for a 'drinkable broth' made from Rishiri kombu, several kinds of dried fish, Noto salt and Ono soy sauce, and makes its own chikuwa, hanpen and fritters in house.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイトとfood-japonで、店主平田賢太郎、2015年8月8日片町開業、『輪を築く』の店名、金沢駅あんと支店、利尻昆布と数種の削り節・大野醤油・能登塩の『飲み干せる出汁』、自家製ちくわ・はんぺん・ごぼう天、いくらのせ卵・揚げ豚・たらこおでん・牛すじ麻婆などの創作を確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: All oden items simmer together in a single shared fish-and-soy dashi pot, so even non-wheat items share the broth.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The broth is seasoned with local soy sauce, which standardly contains wheat; house-made fish cakes (chikuwa, hanpen, fritters) are also typically wheat-bound surimi.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The base dashi is made from bonito and dried fish, so all simmered items — including vegetables — are cooked in animal stock.

positives.text: Dashi and fish cakes are made fresh in house daily, so staff know exactly what goes into each item and can be asked about ingredients in person.

cultural_comfort.note: A cozy local oden counter where a few words of Japanese and a friendly greeting go a long way; pointing at items and asking what's in them works fine for a curious foreign student.

kz_kanmidokoro_kinkato.gf_detail: Not a gluten-free destination. Many items are naturally wheat-free at their core (anko from Tamba Dainagon beans, shiratama mochi made from rice flour, agar/kanten, kuzukiri, homemade ice cream, anmitsu syrup), so a careful gluten-avoider may find suitable choices. However nothing is certified GF, the kitchen is not dedicated, and shared utensils/cross-contact are likely. No documented allergen handling. Celiac travelers should ask directly and not assume safety.
kz_kanmidokoro_kinkato.vegan_detail: A few items appear plant-based in principle (anmitsu with anko, shiratama, kanten and fruit; kuzukiri), but the signature sweets are typically served with homemade dairy ice cream, and items like zenzai or toppings may contain dairy. No vegan menu or labeling exists. A vegan would need to ask whether ice cream/dairy can be omitted; assume options are limited and must be confirmed in person.
kz_kanmidokoro_kinkato.hours_raw: 12:00 until dusk (noon until dusk; sources list closing around 17:00). Closed Tue and the 3rd Wed.
kz_kanmidokoro_kinkato.notes: [Mom & Pop] 甘味処 金花糖 is a small, personally-run sweets house set inside a renovated former residence with a gate-like entrance, hidden down a side lane just off the canal-lined street in Kanazawa's Nagamachi samurai district. Diners sit in a quiet, deeply Japanese interior and can take in a s

chef_bio.background: 甘味処 金花糖 is a small, personally-run sweets house set inside a renovated former residence in Kanazawa's Nagamachi samurai district, reached by turning down a side lane just off the canal-lined street. Diners sit in a quiet, deeply Japanese (純和風) interior; older accounts describe the warm, old-house atmosphere.
chef_bio.philosophy: A slow, my-pace approach to traditional Japanese sweets, with an emphasis on homemade components and quality ingredients (the fruit for the cream anmitsu is sourced from Fruits Sakano in Omicho Market).
chef_bio.specialty: Almost everything except the fruit is made in-house: the anko (red bean paste) from Tamba Dainagon beans, the shiratama dumplings, the kanten, and the ice cream. Signature dishes are the cream anmitsu piled with fruit and the tea/Earl-Grey anmitsu served with an orange-liqueur-scented white syrup; uji-kintoki shaved ice, kuzukiri and (winter) zenzai also appear on the menu.

anecdotes.text: The cream anmitsu is built on fruit from the Fruits Sakano greengrocer in Omicho Market, paired with fluffy Tamba Dainagon bean paste and the shop's homemade ice cream.
Reviewers describe it as a my-pace sweets shop reached by turning one lane off the canal-lined road through the Nagamachi samurai-residence district.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelogで、長町の旧家を改装した純和風の甘味処、丹波大納言の自家製餡・白玉・寒天・アイス（フルーツ以外は自家製）、近江町のフルーツ坂野の果物を使うクリームあんみつ、紅茶あんみつ（オレンジリキュール香る白蜜）、宇治金時、くずきりを確認。冬季はぜんざい。

vegan_cross_contact.text: Signature anmitsu dishes are typically served with the shop's homemade dairy ice cream, so plant-based diners should ask for it to be omitted.

positives.text: Core components are made in-house (anko from Tamba Dainagon beans, shiratama, kanten, ice cream), so ingredients are simple and known to the makers.

cultural_comfort.note: A tiny, traditional family-run sweets house tucked down a lane in the Nagamachi samurai district where the owners offer warm Kanazawa-dialect hospitality, so a little Japanese (or a pointing finger at the menu) goes a long way and English help is not guaranteed.

kz_tsubomi.gf_detail: Several signature sweets are starch-based rather than wheat-based — honkuzukiri is made from premium Yoshino arrowroot (kudzu) starch and the honwarabimochi from bracken starch with kinako and kuromitsu — so they are inherently low in wheat. However, the kitchen documents no celiac-safe handling, no dedicated equipment, and items like anmitsu/zenzai and seasonal toppings may involve shared utensils or wheat-containing components. Celiacs should confirm each item directly; this is not a certified gluten-free venue.
kz_tsubomi.vegan_detail: Many items are plant-leaning — kuzukiri, warabimochi, sweet-potato zenzai and anmitsu are built around starches, red beans, kinako and kuromitsu — but parfaits and cream anmitsu include dairy, and no dish is labeled vegan. Dashi or other animal-derived elements in some items are not ruled out. Vegans should ask item by item.
kz_tsubomi.notes: [Mom & Pop] Tsubomi opened in 2004 in the Kakinokibatake district near the 21st Century Museum of Art, founded by the long-established Kanazawa kaiseki ryotei Honami (穂濤). At the time, a ryotei operating a dedicated sweets shop was said to be the first attempt of its kind in Japan. The café

chef_bio.background: Tsubomi opened in 2004 in the Kakinokibatake district near the 21st Century Museum of Art, founded by the long-established Kanazawa kaiseki ryotei Honami (穂濤). At the time, a ryotei operating a dedicated sweets shop was said to be the first attempt of its kind in Japan. The café grew out of the popularity of the kuzukiri dessert served at the parent restaurant, conceived as an approachable way to introduce guests to kaiseki culture.
chef_bio.philosophy: Owner Koichiro Koshikawa describes the aim as serving the finest ingredients in the finest setting (最高の材料を、最高の場所で食べてもらうこと), personally visiting producers and selecting specific farms — for example a particular grower of Goroshima-kintoki sweet potatoes — rather than accepting any supplier.
chef_bio.specialty: Honkuzukiri — delicate, translucent arrowroot noodles made from the highest-grade Yoshino kudzu, served with kuromitsu black molasses — alongside honwarabimochi from premium bracken starch with kinako, white-dumpling cream anmitsu, kintoki sweet-potato zenzai, and limited summer kakigori such as the popular white-peach shaved ice. Every sweet comes with complimentary Kanazawa bocha roasted tea.

anecdotes.text: The shop's earthen walls were finished by Kanazawa plasterers over roughly three months, and the space is built around a single large wooden slab table.

The courtyard garden borrows the stone walls of Kanazawa Castle's outer moat as scenery, with the sound of the historic Tatsumi waterway running nearby and seasonal mountain plants marking the seasons.
Honami's kuzukiri was so popular at the main restaurant that the owner created Tsubomi to share it more accessibly — reportedly the first time a ryotei in Japan opened its own sweets shop.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: かなめ金沢とことりっぷで、2004年開業、料亭穂濤が母体、料亭による甘味処は日本初とされる、最高級吉野本葛の本くずきり、越沢晃一郎氏、五郎島金時の生産者指定、左官職人が約3か月で仕上げた土壁・一枚板の大テーブル、金沢城石垣の借景と辰巳用水、ほうじ茶（棒茶）付きを確認。

positives.text: Several signature sweets are naturally starch-based rather than wheat-based: honkuzukiri is made from Yoshino arrowroot (kudzu) and honwarabimochi from bracken starch, with kinako and kuromitsu.

cultural_comfort.note: A calm, traditional sweets café where a few words of Japanese and a relaxed manner go a long way; menus are simple and pointing works, but English support is limited.

kz_wagashi_murakami_kanazaw.gf_detail: Not gluten-free safe by default. While some wagashi are rice-based (mochi/anko), the signature ふくさ餅 has a soft baked skin made with wheat flour, and many traditional sweets and the café menu (mont blanc, soft serve) involve wheat and dairy. No celiac-safe protocols are documented; cross-contamination in a shared confectionery kitchen is likely. A traveler avoiding gluten would need to ask item-by-item and should not assume safety.
kz_wagashi_murakami_kanazaw.vegan_detail: Some core wagashi (mochi with red bean paste, 黒糖ふくさ餅, わり氷) are plant-based by tradition, but ingredients are not labeled vegan and the eat-in menu includes dairy items (soft serve ice cream, mont blanc). No vegan certification or stated egg/dairy-free assurances are documented, so a vegan should confirm ingredients per item before ordering.
kz_wagashi_murakami_kanazaw.notes: 和菓子 村上 was founded in Kanazawa in 1911 (Meiji 44) and has spent more than a century devoted to a single path of sweets-making. The Nagamachi shop in central Kanazawa sits near the historic samurai district, pairing a confectionery counter with a sit-down café (菓ふぇ MURAKAMI) where

chef_bio.background: 和菓子 村上 was founded in Kanazawa in 1911 (Meiji 44) and has spent more than a century devoted to a single path of sweets-making. The Nagamachi shop in central Kanazawa sits near the historic samurai district, pairing a confectionery counter with a sit-down café (菓ふぇ MURAKAMI) where visitors can rest between sightseeing.
chef_bio.philosophy: The house holds that 'the foundation of wagashi is delicious bean paste' (和菓子の基本は、美味しい餡づくりから), insisting on homemade filling and traditional technique carried on unchanged since its founding.
chef_bio.specialty: The signature ふくさ餅 wraps mochi and house-made bean paste in a soft baked skin; the black-sugar 黒糖ふくさ餅 is a classic Kanazawa souvenir. The eat-in café is also known for a honten-limited gold-leaf azuki soft serve, chestnut mont blanc, and seasonal wagashi such as 垣穂 (kinako and sesame) and the crystalline dry sweet わり氷.

anecdotes.text: Founded in 1911 (Meiji 44), the maker has dedicated itself to a single path of confectionery for over a century, prizing homemade bean paste above all.
The black-sugar fukusa mochi — mochi and house-made anko wrapped in a fluffy black-sugar skin — is treated as a quintessential Kanazawa souvenir.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイトとたびいろで、明治44年（1911）創業、『和菓子の基本は美味しい餡づくりから』の信条、名物ふくさ餅と金沢土産の定番黒糖ふくさ餅、本店限定の金箔あずきソフト、和栗のモンブラン、銘菓垣穂（きなこ・黒胡麻）、干菓子わり氷を確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Shared confectionery kitchen producing wheat-based sweets (the baked-skin ふくさ餅) alongside other items; no gluten-free protocol documented.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Eat-in menu mixes plant-based wagashi with dairy items (soft serve, mont blanc); no separation or vegan labeling documented.

positives.text: Some traditional offerings such as mochi with red bean paste and the dry sweet わり氷 are naturally plant-based.

cultural_comfort.note: A welcoming traditional sweets shop with an eat-in café where a smile and a few words of Japanese go a long way; pointing at the display cases works fine.

kz_los_angeles_organic_natu.gf_detail: Not a dedicated gluten-free kitchen, but there are real GF options: the daily-baked vegan muffins are made with rice flour and described as gluten-free, and gluten-free sweets are highlighted. The savory menu (soy-based "meat" burgers, teriyaki/ginger items) likely involves wheat-containing seasonings such as soy sauce and breaded/wheat-based mock meats, so celiac diners should ask item-by-item. No statement about a dedicated fryer or cross-contamination controls was found.
kz_los_angeles_organic_natu.vegan_detail: Fully vegan / 100% plant-based. The owner states the food contains absolutely no meat, eggs, dairy, or animal-derived fats, and all dressings are homemade and animal-free. Centered on Kaga vegetables (Kanazawa shungiku chrysanthemum greens, Kaga lotus root) and other organic/pesticide-free local vegetables, with soy-based meat alternatives and pesticide-free Isehikari rice.
kz_los_angeles_organic_natu.hours_raw: Mon & Thu 10:00-16:00; Tue, Wed, Fri, Sat 10:00-17:00; Sun closed. Lunch service roughly 11:30-14:00. (A local guide lists broader 10:00-18:00 with irregular closures, so confirm before visiting.)
kz_los_angeles_organic_natu.notes: Los Angeles is a fully plant-based cafe in central Kanazawa, opened in 2014. Owner Mikihiro Morishima evacuated from Iwaki City in Fukushima to Ishikawa after the disaster and built the cafe around a wish to share the safe, delicious vegetables that local farmers work hard to gro

chef_bio.background: Los Angeles is a fully plant-based cafe in central Kanazawa (Otemachi), opened in 2014. Owner Mikihiro Morishima evacuated from Iwaki City in Fukushima to Ishikawa after the disaster and built the cafe around a wish to share the safe, delicious vegetables that local farmers work hard to grow. Everything served is vegan, containing no meat, eggs, dairy, or animal fats.
chef_bio.philosophy: The cafe describes a 'New Smart Life Style' where dining is about more than taste - caring for your own and your family's wellbeing, the environment, and connection with others, summed up in the line 'Luxury is satisfaction of the soul.' Vegetables are sourced from pesticide-free local growers such as Tomofarm and Eco Farm Okuno.
chef_bio.specialty: The signature Veggie Combination Lunch is a large wooden bowl piled with Kaga vegetables such as Kanazawa shungiku chrysanthemum greens and Kaga lotus root alongside many seasonal organic greens, paired with soy-based 'meat' dishes like a ginger steak bowl or burger and pesticide-free Isehikari rice. Soy-meat ginger steak and teriyaki burgers are popular, and the daily handmade gluten-free rice-flour vegan muffins (2-3 kinds) often sell out as soon as they hit the counter. (As always for celiac guests, confirm current handling directly with the cafe.)

anecdotes.text: Owner Mikihiro Morishima relocated from Fukushima's Iwaki City to Ishikawa after evacuating, opening Los Angeles to introduce people to the safe, tasty vegetables grown by local farmers.
The gluten-free rice-flour vegan muffins are baked fresh every day in 2-3 varieties and frequently sell out right after they appear on the counter.
The logo artwork was created by designer Sarah Williams, who previously worked on art for Cirque du Soleil's 'Viva Elvis!' production.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: ことりっぷと公式コンセプトページで、店主森島幹裕（いわき市から避難）、2014年開業、肉・卵・乳・動物性油脂不使用の完全植物性、加賀野菜、ヴィーガンのベジコンビランチ、大豆ミートの生姜焼き・バーガー、伊勢ひかり米、トモファーム/エコファーム奥野、毎日2〜3種の米粉グルテンフリー・ヴィーガンマフィン（即完売）、ロゴはサラ・ウィリアムズ（シルク・ドゥ・ソレイユ Viva Elvis）を確認。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Savory items include teriyaki and ginger 'steak' preparations made with soy-based mock meat; these typically involve wheat-containing soy sauce/seasonings, so celiac diners should confirm each dish rather than assume it is gluten-free.

positives.text: Fully vegan kitchen with no meat, eggs, dairy, or animal fats, and homemade animal-free dressings - very low risk of accidental animal ingredients.
Daily handmade gluten-free vegan muffins are made with rice flour, and gluten-free sweets are a regular offering.
Vegetables come from named pesticide-free local farms (Tomofarm, Eco Farm Okuno) and include Kaga vegetables, with pesticide-free Isehikari rice.

cultural_comfort.note: A small, welcoming plant-based cafe where a little Japanese helps; the fully vegan menu and takeout make it easy for a foreign student, though staff English may be limited so a few polite phrases go a long way.

kz_ichiba_meshi_amatsubo.gf_detail: Not gluten-free friendly. The kitchen is built around Kanazawa oden simmered in a soy-and-dashi broth, plus tempura, fried fish cakes (satsuma-age, chikuwa) and signature kuruma-fu (wheat gluten), all of which contain wheat. Soy sauce and oden dashi are central to nearly every dish. There is no gluten-free menu and no indication of allergen accommodation, so this is not safe for celiacs.
kz_ichiba_meshi_amatsubo.vegan_detail: This is a seafood and Kaga-cuisine eatery: sashimi, seafood rice bowls (uni, botan shrimp, salmon roe, tuna), and oden built on fish/bonito dashi. Even vegetable items (daikon, konnyaku) are simmered in a fish-based broth, so there is no reliable vegan option.
kz_ichiba_meshi_amatsubo.hours_raw: 8:00-21:00 daily; Wednesday 8:00-15:00 (lunch only). Sources vary slightly on Wednesday — the Omicho Market and official pages list Wednesday 8:00-15:00, while Tabelog lists Wednesday as closed. Occasional multi-day/year-end closures.
kz_ichiba_meshi_amatsubo.notes: Amatsubo was founded in 1964 (Showa 39) by the current owner's parents, who first set up in Kanazawa's Korinbo district before moving to Kakinokibata in 1984. Curiously, oden was not on the menu at the start: the shop originally ran with two entrances and two signboards, operatin

chef_bio.background: Amatsubo was founded in 1964 (Showa 39) in Kanazawa's Korinbo district by the current proprietor's parents, moving to Kakinokibata in 1984 and now run by the founders' son (the Amatsubo / 雨坪 family). Curiously, oden was not on the menu at the start: the shop originally ran with two entrances and two signboards, operating as both a popular diner (taishu-shokudo) and a Western-style restaurant. The founder added oden only later, in response to customers' requests. This market-side branch, 市場めし あまつぼ, brings the honten's flavors right into Omicho Market, Kanazawa's centuries-old 'kitchen.'
chef_bio.philosophy: Showcasing fresh Kaga and Noto ingredients in hearty, approachable Kanazawa home-cooking, open from early morning so visitors can enjoy oden and local sake any time of day.
chef_bio.specialty: Kanazawa oden (signature items include kuruma-fu / wheat-gluten and well-simmered daikon) in a clear kombu-and-bonito dashi seasoned simply with Noto salt and sake, plus generous market-fresh kaisendon seafood rice bowls topped with uni, botan shrimp, salmon roe and tuna, sashimi, and Kaga dishes such as duck jibu-ni.

anecdotes.text: The shop did not serve oden at first — it originally had two entrances and operated as both a popular diner and a Western restaurant; the founder (the current owner's father) added oden only after customers asked for it.
Amatsubo belongs to the Kanazawa Oden 50-Year Veterans Association, whose rules are that oden ingredients use local Kanazawa products and that the oden is available year-round.
A longtime community fixture beloved by Kanazawa University alumni and Ishikawa prefectural staff, the shop has run for over 50 years.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: ことりっぷ・iいじ金沢・週末金沢と検索で、1964年香林坊で創業（現社長の両親）、1984年柿木畠へ移転、創業当初は入口2つ・大衆食堂と洋食屋の2枚看板でおでんは後から客の要望で追加、金沢おでん老舗50年会（地元食材・通年提供）、車麩・大根、昆布とカツオに能登塩・酒の透き通る出汁を確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Oden broth is soy-sauce and dashi based and shared across all simmered items; fried items (tempura, satsuma-age, chikuwa) and wheat-gluten kuruma-fu are core menu items, so wheat contact is pervasive.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Standard Japanese soy sauce (contains wheat) is central to the oden broth and seafood-bowl seasoning; no wheat-free tamari indicated.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Even vegetable oden items (daikon, konnyaku) are simmered in a fish/bonito-based dashi shared with seafood and meat items.

cultural_comfort.note: A bustling, casual market eatery where pointing at the picture menu and a friendly "konnichiwa" will carry you through; staff are used to tourists but English is limited, so a few basic Japanese words help.

kz_grill_otsuka.gf_detail: Not gluten-free friendly. The kitchen is built around breaded/fried items (marlin and shrimp fries), omelette-over-rice with ketchup, hamburg steak, cream croquettes and flour-based cream/white sauces — all wheat-heavy. No gluten-free menu, no dedicated fryer, and shared frying oil makes this unsafe for celiacs.
kz_grill_otsuka.vegan_detail: Not vegan-friendly. The menu centers on seafood (fried marlin/swordfish, shrimp), eggs (the signature dish uses about three eggs per plate), meat (hamburg, pork steak) and dairy-based cream sauces and soups. No vegan options are documented.
kz_grill_otsuka.hours_raw: 11:00-15:20 (L.O. 14:45), 17:00-20:30 (L.O. 19:50). Closed Wednesday (open if Wed is a holiday, with Thursday as substitute holiday). One additional temporary closure per month.
kz_grill_otsuka.notes: [Mom & Pop] A brick-fronted Western-style diner (yoshoku) founded in 1957 by Taduzou Otsuka. It is now run by the third generation, Masaki Otsuka, who took over from his father and second-generation owner Shoji Otsuka.
