cultural_comfort.note: A tiny, warmly personal owner-run café in a hidden machiya; the owner happily chats with first-time guests, but there's no indication of English service, so a few basic Japanese phrases will help a foreign student feel at ease.

kz_kappo_matsuyoshi.gf_detail: Traditional Kaga kappo built around dashi, soy sauce, and simmered/braised preparations. No gluten-free menu or accommodations are documented, and wheat-based soy sauce is integral to the cuisine (e.g. jibuni, simmered dishes). Not suitable for celiacs.
kz_kappo_matsuyoshi.vegan_detail: A seafood-forward Kaga cuisine restaurant; signature dishes include grilled fish, snow crab, and jibuni (a meat/poultry stew). Dashi is fish/kombu based. No vegan or vegetarian menu is documented.
kz_kappo_matsuyoshi.hours_raw: Monday-Saturday 17:30-22:00; closed Sundays (plus occasional irregular closures).
kz_kappo_matsuyoshi.notes: [Mom & Pop] Founded in 1979, Matsuyoshi is a kappo tucked onto Daikumachi, a quiet side street one block back from busy Katamachi and within walking distance of Korinbo and the Omicho market. The restaurant was built by first-generation owner Akira Matsushita, who set famously strict standar

chef_bio.background: Founded more than four decades ago, Matsuyoshi is a kappo tucked onto Daikumachi, a quiet side street one block back from busy Katamachi and within walking distance of Korinbo and the Omicho market. The restaurant was built by the first-generation Matsushita, who set famously strict standards for taste and presentation. After his passing, his sons carried it on as a brother team; the current chef-owner, Matsushita Motohisa, trained at kappo restaurants in Kyoto and Osaka before returning home to continue the family tradition.
chef_bio.philosophy: An uncompromising commitment to delicate, gentle flavors and refined seasonal presentation, letting Ishikawa's abundant ingredients speak for themselves.
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal Kaga cuisine sourced daily from the market and prepared through slow simmering, resting, and flavor-infusion. Signature offerings include seasonal steamed dishes in a delicate sauce, a clear seasonal broth built on Ishikawa ingredients, and stone-grilled beef.

anecdotes.text: The first-generation Matsushita was known for an exceptionally strict, no-compromise approach to flavor, and his sons — including current chef-owner Matsushita Motohisa — trained in Kyoto and Osaka before returning to preserve that reputation among regulars and connoisseurs.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: hitosara は現店主・松下素久(1987年石川生)が京都・大阪の割烹で修業し、兄弟で先代の加賀料理を継承、席数25、蒸し物・お椀・肉の石焼を提供、と確認。gorp(公式)は先代の妥協なき味へのこだわりと市場での毎日の仕入れ・煮る/寝かせる/含ませる工程を裏付け。創業1979年と先代の下の名前は未確認のためぼかした。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Traditional Kaga cuisine relies on wheat-based soy sauce and dashi in simmered and braised dishes such as jibuni; no gluten-free preparation is documented.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Menu is seafood- and meat-forward (grilled fish, snow crab, jibuni stew) with fish/kombu dashi throughout; no vegan offerings are documented.

cultural_comfort.note: This is a refined, reservation-only kappo where most communication is in Japanese and dinner runs around 10,000 yen and up, so it suits a student comfortable ordering in Japanese for a special occasion rather than a casual drop-in.

kz_kawaki_shoten.gf_detail: Not gluten-free friendly. The signature kabayaki sauce is built on Ohno soy sauce (regular Japanese soy sauce contains wheat) plus malt syrup, brushed onto the grilled eel and loach. This is a soy-sauce-and-seafood shop with no gluten-free accommodation documented, so it is not celiac-safe.
kz_kawaki_shoten.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The entire shop is built around animal products: charcoal-grilled eel and loach, crab, oysters, sea urchin, scallops, and shrimp. There are no documented plant-based options.
kz_kawaki_shoten.hours_raw: Approx. 9:00–15:30 (shop ~8:30–16:00 for crab; eel grilling from around 9:00–9:30). Eel not served on Wednesdays.
kz_kawaki_shoten.notes: [Mom & Pop] Kawaki Shoten is one of the long-standing crab-and-eel specialists in Kanazawa's Omicho Market, run as a family business (有限会社 川木商店). It sits on the ground floor of the Omicho Ichiba-kan building, where the family grills eel and loach over charcoal right at the stall and sells cr

chef_bio.background: Kawaki Shoten is one of the long-standing crab-and-eel specialists in Kanazawa's Omicho Market, run as a family business (有限会社 川木商店). It sits on the ground floor of the Omicho Ichiba-kan building, where the family grills eel and loach over charcoal right at the stall and sells crab, oysters, sea urchin, scallops and shrimp from the same counter.
chef_bio.philosophy: The shop is particular about origin, sauce and grilling method: eels with firm flesh are grilled hot and fast over domestic charcoal to seal in the umami, rested for about an hour, then dipped and grilled again so the sauce soaks in — leaving crisp skin and fluffy flesh.
chef_bio.specialty: Charcoal-grilled unagi (eel) kabayaki and the more unusual, very affordable dojo (loach) kabayaki at around 100-120 yen a skewer, alongside boiled crab and seasonal Kanazawa seafood like nodoguro and rock oysters.

anecdotes.text: The kabayaki sauce has been kept going and replenished for over 50 years since the shop's founding, made with Ohno soy sauce and malt syrup for a rounded umami without an aggressive edge.
Eels are sourced from Aichi Prefecture for their firm flesh and grilled over domestic charcoal at high heat for a short time, then rested and re-grilled with the sauce.
The loach kabayaki is glazed with a slightly sweeter sauce than the eel and sold for about 120 yen a skewer, making it an easy, cheap taste of an old Kanazawa specialty.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kanazawabiyori は、愛知県産うなぎ・国産炭で高温短時間→約1時間休ませて再度タレ焼き・大野醤油と水飴の継ぎ足しダレ(50年以上)・どじょう蒲焼き120円(うなぎより甘めのタレ)を確認。ohmicho-ichiba は近江町いちば館1階の店舗であることを裏付け。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Everything is grilled and glazed on a shared charcoal kabayaki setup with a wheat-containing soy-sauce glaze; no gluten-free preparation is offered.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The signature kabayaki sauce is made with Ohno soy sauce and malt syrup; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, so the eel and loach glaze is not gluten-free.

vegan_cross_contact.text: This is a crab, eel, loach and shellfish stall with no plant-based menu items, so cross-contact with animal products is unavoidable.

cultural_comfort.note: A bustling market stall where you point at what you want and eat grilled eel or loach skewers standing up — easy and welcoming, but expect Japanese-only service, so it helps to know the dish names or come with a guide.

kz_oden_ebisu.gf_detail: Not celiac-safe. The house oden is built on a continuously-replenished bonito-and-kombu dashi typically seasoned with wheat-based soy sauce, and the menu centers on oden, sashimi, and obanzai such as char siu — all high cross-contamination risk. No gluten-free accommodation is documented.
kz_oden_ebisu.vegan_detail: Not vegan-friendly. This is a seafood-and-meat oden/izakaya: bonito dashi broth, sashimi, shellfish oden, and char siu are core offerings. Some vegetable obanzai or oden items (daikon, ginkgo) exist but are simmered in fish-based dashi. No vegan menu is documented.
kz_oden_ebisu.notes: [Mom & Pop] Ebisu has stood near Omicho Market, Kanazawa's centuries-old kitchen, since 1966 (Showa 41), making it one of the city's long-running oden institutions — well over half a century of service to local regulars.

chef_bio.origin: 西町藪ノ内通, a few minutes from Omicho Market in central Kanazawa.
chef_bio.background: Ebisu has stood near Omicho Market, Kanazawa's centuries-old kitchen, since 1966 (Showa 41), making it one of the city's long-running oden institutions — well over half a century of service to local regulars.
chef_bio.philosophy: Daily selection of quality ingredients from neighboring Omicho Market and a generations-deep dashi are the heart of the kitchen; the small counter is meant to feel, as one writer put it, warming to the heart.
chef_bio.specialty: Kanazawa-style oden simmered in a bonito-and-Rishiri-kombu dashi that has been continuously replenished since the shop opened, with notably large oden pieces — daikon, shinoda-maki, shellfish, ginkgo, beef tendon — alongside an abundant, seasonally rotating lineup of home-style obanzai dishes and fresh sashimi sourced daily at the market.

anecdotes.text: The oden broth carries the shop's whole history: a bonito and kombu dashi continuously topped up since the 1966 opening, soaking into each oversized oden piece.
An intimate counter-only room that fills daily with knowledgeable local regulars seeking specific seasonal obanzai — grilled pork, vinegared vegetables, tempura — beyond the oden itself.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kanazawa.cc は昭和41年(1966)創業・継ぎ足しの鰹と昆布のダシ・L字カウンター全17席・地元常連・とろける焼豚や刺身などのおばんざいを確認。iijikanazawa は西町藪ノ内通の住所・鰹と利尻昆布の継ぎ足しダシ・大ぶりのしのだ巻きや貝などのおでん種を裏付け。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Menu is oden, sashimi, and obanzai cooked in a shared bonito-kombu dashi with wheat-based soy sauce and served in a tiny counter kitchen; cross-contamination risk is high and no gluten-free handling is documented.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Kanazawa oden and obanzai are conventionally seasoned with wheat-containing soy sauce; no wheat-free tamari is mentioned.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Core broth is bonito (fish) dashi and the menu features sashimi, shellfish, and char siu, so even vegetable items are simmered in animal-based stock.

cultural_comfort.note: A tiny, regulars-filled local oden counter where some Japanese helps and a phone call ahead is wise, since seating is limited and the place is sometimes described as favoring familiar faces.

kz_musubi_omicho_ichiba_ten.gf_detail: Not gluten-free safe. This is a handmade onigiri (rice ball) stand. While plain salt, umeboshi (pickled plum), or kombu rice balls are naturally rice-based, the shop also sells croquettes (wheat breading) and uses soy sauce-based fillings, and there is no allergen separation or dedicated equipment at this small open stall. No gluten-free handling is documented. Not suitable for celiacs.
kz_musubi_omicho_ichiba_ten.vegan_detail: A few onigiri may be plant-based (e.g. plain salt, umeboshi pickled plum, or kombu seaweed), but most fillings are fish, meat, or mayonnaise-based, and rice may be seasoned with dashi (fish/bonito stock). The shop also sells Noto-beef croquettes and other meat items. No vegan menu is documented; vegans should ask which onigiri are free of fish/meat/dashi, and a language barrier should be expected.
kz_musubi_omicho_ichiba_ten.hours_raw: Mon-Fri 08:00-16:00 / Sat, Sun & holidays 10:00-17:00 (closed Wed). Note: the official site lists the Omicho Market branch as 11:00-17:00 with irregular days off.
kz_musubi_omicho_ichiba_ten.notes: [Mom & Pop] Musubi is a handmade rice ball (omusubi) shop that has been making onigiri in Kanazawa for over 20 years. Its main store sits inside JR Kanazawa Station, and this smaller branch stands right at the lively entrance of Omicho Market, the city's centuries-old fresh-food market.

chef_bio.background: Musubi is a handmade rice ball (omusubi) shop that has been making onigiri in Kanazawa for over 20 years. Its main store sits inside JR Kanazawa Station, and this smaller branch stands right at the lively entrance of Omicho Market, the city's centuries-old fresh-food market.
chef_bio.philosophy: The shop's motto, '真心むすびます' (rolled with heartfelt sincerity), reflects its craft approach: rice is cooked over strong gas heat with soft water and washed by hand, then each ball is shaped gently by a craftsperson's hands alone, never with a mold.
chef_bio.specialty: Hand-shaped onigiri made from rice specially chosen for rice balls, alongside croquettes (including a Noto-beef heart-shaped croquette) and gold-leaf soft-serve ice cream that nods to Kanazawa's famous gold leaf.

anecdotes.text: At its peak the company has hand-rolled as many as 8,000 onigiri in a single day, all made for the counter rather than pre-ordered.
The Omicho Market branch leans into local Kanazawa treats, offering a gold-leaf soft serve and a Noto-beef croquette shaped like a heart.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: musubi-co(公式)は創業22年・モットー『真心むすびます』・軟水と強火・職人が型を使わず手で握る・1日最高8,000個・金沢駅と近江町の2店を確認。tabelog は近江町店の金箔ソフト(900円)とハート型能登牛コロッケ(200円)を裏付け。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Wheat-breaded croquettes are sold and fried at the same small stall as the rice products, with no documented separation.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Soy sauce-based onigiri fillings are common at such shops and standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat; no wheat-free soy sauce is documented.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Fish, meat, and mayonnaise fillings are prepared alongside any plain rice balls at the same counter; no separation is documented.

positives.text: Naturally simple options like plain salt, umeboshi (pickled plum), or kombu onigiri may suit some diners, though fillings should be confirmed in person.

cultural_comfort.note: A tiny cash-only grab-and-go onigiri stand at the market entrance with little or no English, so point at what you want and have small bills ready; easiest with a guide or translation app if you need to check fillings.

kz_musubi_soba.gf_detail: Not gluten-free safe. The house soba is 二八 (nihachi) — a buckwheat-and-wheat blend, so the noodles themselves contain wheat. The dashi-based tsuyu broth, tempura batter, and likely soy sauce all add further gluten. There is no documented gluten-free menu or handling, and cross-contamination from shared wheat-flour soba prep is essentially unavoidable. Not suitable for celiacs.
kz_musubi_soba.vegan_detail: No vegan menu is documented. The soba broth is a bonito-and-kombu dashi (contains fish), the onigiri fillings include salmon and Noto pork, and tempura is fried in a shared setting. A plain rice onigiri (e.g., umeboshi) might be obtainable, but there is no confirmed plant-based offering — a vegan would need to ask directly and verify the broth/fillings.
kz_musubi_soba.notes: [Mom & Pop] むすびそば opened in April 2025 on the 2nd floor of かなざわはこまち, a shopping complex about a one-minute walk from the historic Omicho Market in central Kanazawa. It is a specialist shop built around two simple staples: hand-rolled soba and freshly made rice balls (omusubi).

chef_bio.background: むすびそば opened in April 2025 on the 2nd floor of かなざわはこまち, a shopping complex about a one-minute walk from the historic Omicho Market in central Kanazawa. It is a specialist shop built around two simple staples: hand-rolled soba and freshly made rice balls (omusubi).
chef_bio.philosophy: The shop's stated aim is 素朴で優しい美味しさ — a plain, gentle deliciousness in its soba and onigiri. The fuller set menu reportedly grew out of customer requests for something more substantial than soba alone.
chef_bio.specialty: Self-described as 自家製二八蕎麦とおむすびのお店 — a house-made nihachi (80% buckwheat / 20% wheat) soba kneaded and cut in-store using domestic buckwheat flour, served in a bonito-and-kombu dashi. Signature plates include the 海老天そば (shrimp tempura soba) and the むすびそば御膳 set of half-portion soba, onigiri, tempura and a small side. The onigiri come in about six varieties made with Ishikawa-grown rice, including Noto pork with shiso-miso, salmon, and umeboshi.

anecdotes.text: The soba is a nihachi blend made from domestic buckwheat flour and hand-rolled inside the shop each day.
Onigiri are made with Ishikawa-grown rice and cooked fresh daily, in small handheld portions across about six fillings such as Noto pork with shiso-miso.

cultural_comfort.note: A relaxed, modern, family-friendly counter-and-table shop inside a shopping building — easy to walk into, point at the picture menu, and order soba or an onigiri even with only a few words of Japanese.

kz_kadocho_sohonten.gf_detail: This is a wheat-noodle house: udon and soba (soba is typically blended with wheat flour), plus tempura, tonkatsu, and a dashi/sweet-soy broth that contains wheat. There is no gluten-free menu and the kitchen is wheat-heavy, so it is not safe for celiacs.
kz_kadocho_sohonten.vegan_detail: The broth is a Kansai-style fish dashi made from urume sardine, mackerel and bonito, and signature dishes feature duck (kamo jibuni), so the menu is built around animal products. No documented vegan options.

chef_bio.background: Kadocho is widely called Kanazawa's oldest udon shop. The first generation, Wada Chohei, opened the original stall in front of the railway station in Komatsu, and as the rail line pushed north the family followed the tracks and resettled in Kanazawa, where the main shop now stands a short walk from the bustling Omicho Market. Across generations the shop has been a humble neighborhood fixture for well over a century; the third-generation Yoshida Tarokichi revived the business and founded the Kadocho association that at its peak counted more than thirty branches around the city. The main shop reopened in July 2020 after a renovation that added evening service and sake alongside the long-standing lunchtime trade.
chef_bio.philosophy: Hand-made noodles using domestic wheat and an inherited 'kaeshi' base, kept affordable so that locals and travelers can share the same simple, warming bowl.
chef_bio.specialty: Soft, springy 'Kanazawa udon' in a sweet Kansai-style broth blended with Kanazawa's sweet soy sauce; the signature plate is the kamo jibuni set (duck and vegetables simmered with sudare-fu wheat gluten in a sweet-savory sauce, served with udon, salad and mixed rice). Other favorites include mizore udon with grated daikon, bonito and yuzu-kosho, tanuki udon, and Kaga-vegetable tempura.

anecdotes.text: The shop is the root of what is now called Komatsu udon, having literally migrated up the rail line from Komatsu to Kanazawa with the spread of the railway.
Its mochi-mochi soft Kanazawa udon, served near Omicho Market, has been celebrated as a noodle beloved even by literary figures.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: shinise.tv は1897年(明治30)和田長平が小松駅前で創業し鉄道の延伸とともに金沢へ移った由来、看板に六代の店主名、三代目吉田太郎吉が加登長会を興し最盛期30店超、を確認。weekend-kanazawa は2020年7月15日リニューアル(夜営業・酒を追加)・みぞれうどん・鴨じぶを、co-trip は近江町近く・もちもちの金沢うどんを裏付け。世代数は特定不能のためぼかした。

gf_cross_contamination.text: A wheat-noodle kitchen serving udon, soba, tempura and tonkatsu; flour and wheat-based broth are pervasive, making cross-contamination unavoidable for gluten-sensitive diners.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The broth combines Kansai dashi with Kanazawa sweet soy sauce; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Base broth is a fish dashi (urume sardine, mackerel, bonito), so even vegetable dishes are prepared in an animal-stock kitchen.

cultural_comfort.note: A relaxed old-style noodle shop where pointing at the menu and a friendly "konnichiwa" will carry you through; English support is limited and payment is cash only.

kz_fumuro_chaya.gf_detail: Not gluten-free at all — in fact the opposite. The entire shop is built around namafu (生麩), which is fresh WHEAT gluten. The signature shira-tama namafu is essentially pure wheat protein. This is one of the least celiac-safe places imaginable and should be avoided entirely by anyone with celiac disease or wheat allergy.
kz_fumuro_chaya.vegan_detail: Many of the namafu sweets are plant-based: the signature shira-tama namafu is served with anko (red bean paste), kinako (roasted soybean powder), and mitarashi (soy-sauce-based sweet sauce), all of which are vegan. However some items are not — e.g. the soft-serve version (しら玉生麩ソフト) uses soy-milk soft serve which may be vegan, but standard soft serve and certain seasonal items may contain dairy. Vegans should confirm individual toppings/soft-serve. Note: nothing here is gluten-free.
kz_fumuro_chaya.hours_raw: 10:00-17:00 (L.O. 16:15); may close earlier when crowded. Closed year-end/New Year.
kz_fumuro_chaya.notes: Fumuro Chaya is the tea-house and sweets outpost of Fumuroya (不室屋), one of Kanazawa's most storied makers of Kaga-fu (wheat gluten). chef_bio.background: Fumuro Chaya is the tea-house and sweets outpost of Fumuroya (不室屋), one of Kanazawa's most storied makers of Kaga-fu (wheat gluten). The family traces its origin to Fumuro village; Kyuemon settled in Owari-cho (today's main shop) and his heir Rokuemon began making fu around February of Keio 1 (1865), naming the house 'Fumuroya' after the founding village. For over 150 years the company has carried on Edo-period techniques for traditional Kaga-fu — including its famous sudare-fu — while developing new products, and this Higashi Chaya shop lets visitors taste that craft as fresh-gluten sweets in a restored townhouse with a tatami room, veranda, and Kanazawa gold-leaf decoration.
chef_bio.philosophy: A place to rest and savor a single, refined traditional sweet while strolling the historic tea streets — the shop frames itself as a quiet pause in the middle of sightseeing.
chef_bio.specialty: Shira-tama namafu (しら玉生麩) — chewy, mochi-like fresh wheat-gluten dumplings served with a choice of anko (red bean), kinako (roasted soybean flour), or mitarashi (sweet-savory) sauce; plus seasonal namafu sweets such as chilled namafu zenzai in summer and hot kinako-and-black-sugar versions in winter.

anecdotes.text: Fumuroya was founded in Keio 1 (1865) when Rokuemon began producing fu, naming the business after the family's ancestral village of Fumuro.

The shop occupies a restored old townhouse in the Higashi Chaya district and presents its signature shira-tama namafu with three toppings (red bean, roasted soybean flour, and mitarashi sauce) in a traditional tatami setting.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: ja.wikipedia は不室屋が慶応元年(1865)創業・久右衛門が尾張町に居を構え跡継ぎ六右衛門が麩の製造を開始・不室村に因む屋号・すだれ麩・150年以上、を確認。co-trip は東山ひがし茶屋街の町家・畳・金箔・名物しら玉生麩(あん/きな粉/みたらし)・季節の生麩汁粉を裏付け。

gf_cross_contamination.text: The shop's entire concept is namafu — fresh wheat gluten — so wheat is the core ingredient throughout. There is no gluten-free path here; cross-contamination is moot because the food itself is wheat protein.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The mitarashi sauce topping is a soy-sauce-based sweet glaze, which typically contains wheat-derived soy sauce.

positives.text: Several signature options are plant-based: shira-tama namafu with anko (red bean), kinako (soybean flour), or mitarashi are all dairy- and egg-free.

cultural_comfort.note: A relaxed, tourist-friendly tea-district sweet shop with a ticket/QR wait system and table seating, where a few words of Japanese and pointing at the menu will get you a beautiful plate of traditional sweets with ease.

kz_hiramipan_boulangerie_et.gf_detail: This is a wheat-flour boulangerie whose core products are bread, croissants, quiche, croque madame and similar wheat-based dishes. No gluten-free menu or accommodation is documented, and it is not safe for celiac diners.
kz_hiramipan_boulangerie_et.vegan_detail: The kitchen is built around bread, eggs, cheese, béchamel and meat (e.g. croque madame with homemade chicken ham and fried egg, quiche). The morning and lunch sets are vegetable-rich but not vegan — they include egg, dairy and often meat. A vegetarian could likely find some plant-forward sides (salad, carrot rape, ratatouille) or plain bread, but no vegan menu is documented; ask in person.
kz_hiramipan_boulangerie_et.hours_raw: Morning 8:00–11:00 (L.O. 10:30), Lunch & Cafe 12:00–15:30 (some sources note cafe until 18:00; bread retail sales 8:00–18:00). Closed Mondays plus irregular closures announced via SNS.

chef_bio.background: Hiramipan was founded in March 2011 in Kanazawa's Nagamachi district, along the willow-lined Seseragi-dori canal walk. The shop occupies a renovated Taisho-era ironworks (鉄工所跡) wrapped in climbing ivy, with vintage and antique furnishings inside that give it a storybook, Studio-Ghibli-like atmosphere. Founder Takahiro Hirame grew the brand over the years and incorporated it as Hiramipan Co., Ltd. in September 2017, later expanding into related ventures including a creperie, gallery and pizza venue.
chef_bio.philosophy: The team explicitly resists being 'just an ordinary bakery,' treating bread and pastry as a medium for personal vision and design — comparable to how an illustrator uses a picture book or a designer uses clothing — and aiming to avoid generic, 'tacky' bread.
chef_bio.specialty: House-baked bread (croissants, melon pan, scones, canelés including the local 金澤カヌレ) and vegetable-rich morning sets — the croque madame set with homemade chicken ham, bechamel and cheddar topped with a fried egg is the signature, alongside quiche and avocado toast sets; lunch plates pair French bistro fare with salad, carrot rape and ratatouille.

anecdotes.text: The shop is set in a renovated Taisho-era ironworks covered in ivy on Seseragi-dori, an aesthetic so distinctive it is often compared to a Studio Ghibli film.
The croque madame is a destination dish — guests come specifically for it at the 8:00 morning service.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: hiramipan.co.jp(公式)は2011年3月創業・2017年9月1日に株式会社ひらみぱん設立・代表平見高広・大正期の鉄工所跡のリノベ・『ただのパン屋にはなりたくない/絵本作家の絵本や服飾デザイナーの服と同じ・ダサいパンは作らない』・クレープリー/ギャラリー/ピザ店を展開、を確認。food-japon はジブリ的な外観とクロックマダム/朝8時の朝食を裏付け。

gf_cross_contamination.text: A working boulangerie where wheat flour is used throughout for bread, croissants, quiche crust and bechamel; airborne flour and shared surfaces make this unsuitable for celiac diners.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Core dishes use egg, dairy (cheddar, bechamel) and meat (homemade chicken ham); shared kitchen and bakery equipment, no documented vegan separation.

positives.text: Morning and lunch sets are notably vegetable-forward, including salad, carrot rape and ratatouille alongside the mains.

cultural_comfort.note: A casual, popular cafe-bakery where ordering is simple and pointing at the bread case works; a little Japanese helps but a friendly greeting and gestures will get you through.

kz_teuchi_soba_hoyasake.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. The core menu is soba (buckwheat noodle flour is typically cut with wheat) and wheat udon, served with dashi/soy-based tsuyu that normally contains wheat. No gluten-free preparation or allergen handling is documented; not safe for celiacs.
kz_teuchi_soba_hoyasake.vegan_detail: Not a vegan destination. Soba and udon are served in bonito/kombu dashi-based broths (typically containing fish stock) with wheat-based soy sauce, and tempura is offered. A plain dish such as cold zaru soba might be possible but the dipping sauce almost certainly contains fish dashi, so vegans must ask in detail and should not assume anything is suitable.
kz_teuchi_soba_hoyasake.notes: [Mom & Pop] A small, owner-run handmade-soba shop tucked into a quaint traditional machiya (wooden townhouse) in Kanazawa's historic Higashi Chaya geisha district, a short walk from Kenrokuen and Kanazawa Castle.

chef_bio.background: A small, owner-run handmade-soba shop of about 29 seats (counter, tables, and a 2nd-floor tatami room), set in a quaint traditional machiya (wooden townhouse) in Kanazawa's Higashiyama / Higashi Chaya area, northeast of Kanazawa Castle across the Asano River.
chef_bio.specialty: Hand-cut soba and Kanazawa-style udon; the kitchen is noted for thin, light-textured wheat udon, alongside cold soba, mountain-yam (tororo) dishes, and kakiage tempura.

anecdotes.text: Tucked into the Higashiyama/Higashi Chaya area behind an old-fashioned machiya facade, the shop takes no reservations and serves noodles only until the day's batch sells out.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: tabelog は東山(ひがし茶屋街)の一軒家・町家・全29席(カウンター9/テーブル4/2階座敷16)・手打ち蕎麦と金沢風の細い小麦うどん・とろろ・かき揚げ・冷たい蕎麦・予約不可・売り切れ仕舞い、を確認。gnavi は店の基本情報を裏付け。店主名は未公開。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Broths and dipping sauces are dashi/soy-based and not specified as wheat-free; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Noodle broths typically use bonito (fish) dashi; no vegan or plant-based broth is documented.

cultural_comfort.note: A tiny, walk-in-only neighborhood soba house in a traditional machiya; staff likely speak little to no English, so point at the menu, bring cash, and be ready for the simple counter-and-tatami atmosphere.

kz_omicho_shokusho_sensai_e.gf_detail: This is a seafood restaurant whose dishes rely heavily on soy sauce (which contains wheat) for sashimi, kaisen-don and hitsumabushi, plus the nodoguro hitsumabushi tea-broth course. No gluten-free menu or celiac handling is documented. Not suitable for strict gluten-free or celiac diners without direct confirmation, and even then cross-contact in a busy market kitchen is likely.
kz_omicho_shokusho_sensai_e.vegan_detail: A fresh-fish-shop-run seafood specialist (sashimi bowls, sushi, nodoguro). Core offerings are fish and shellfish, and dashi/soy-based seasonings are used throughout. No vegan or vegetarian options are documented; not a suitable choice for plant-based diners.
kz_omicho_shokusho_sensai_e.hours_raw: Mon-Fri 11:00-14:00, 17:00-22:00; Sat-Sun 10:00-14:00, 17:00-22:00 (Tabelog). Official site lists lunch 11:00-15:00 (L.O. 14:30) and dinner 17:00-21:00 (L.O. 20:00); hours may vary with ingredient availability.

It is directly run by Okuguchi Suisan, a fresh-fish wholesaler and shop within the same market, so the restaurant draws on the company's daily access to local

roles: Directly run by the Ōguchi Suisan (大口水産) group, a fresh-fish vendor in Omicho Market
chef_bio.origin: Located within 近江町いちば館 in Omicho Market, the centuries-old fish-and-produce market that locals call Kanazawa's kitchen.
chef_bio.background: Sensai Enishi is a seafood eatery on the 2nd floor of the Omicho Ichiba building inside Kanazawa's lively Omicho Market. It is directly run by Ōguchi Suisan (大口水産), a fresh-fish wholesaler and shop within the same market, so the restaurant draws on the company's daily access to local catch from the Sea of Japan.
chef_bio.philosophy: Reflecting the market's hospitality tradition, the operator emphasizes おまけ (generous complimentary extras) and offering high freshness at good value to both tourists and locals.
chef_bio.specialty: Two signature dishes define the menu: the Kaisen Enishi-don, a bowl piled with around 13 kinds of seafood such as tuna, nodoguro (blackthroat seaperch), uni, salmon roe, yellowtail, crab and sweet shrimp; and the Nodoguro Hitsumabushi, which uses a whole prized nodoguro and is eaten three ways - first with wasabi and soy, then mixed with uni and garnishes, and finally as ochazuke with a special broth made from the nodoguro bones.

anecdotes.text: The Kaisen Enishi-don is recommended to be eaten in stages: first enjoy the sashimi toppings dipped in soy sauce, then drizzle wasabi-mixed soy over the rice and seafood for the rest of the bowl.
The nodoguro hitsumabushi uses an entire nodoguro and ends with a tea-over-rice course using broth simmered from the fish's bones.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: enishioumicho.gorp(公式)は『大口水産グループの直営店』であること・のどぐろひつまぶしを3杯(わさび醤油→ウニ+大葉/胡麻→のど黒の骨出汁の茶漬け)・市場のおまけサービスを確認。co-trip はのど黒一尾使用と骨出汁の茶漬け、weekend-kanazawa は海鮮えにし丼(約13種)と段階的な食べ方を裏付け。運営名は『Okuguchi』ではなく大口水産に訂正。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Sashimi bowls, sushi and the hitsumabushi are served and eaten with soy sauce, which standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat; no wheat-free soy alternative is documented.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The kitchen is a dedicated seafood operation run by a fish wholesaler; all signature dishes are fish or shellfish, so cross-contact with animal products is unavoidable.

positives.text: English and Korean menus are available, which can help diners ask about ingredients.

cultural_comfort.note: Easy for foreign students: it is a tourist-friendly market restaurant with English and Korean menus, card and e-money payment, and walk-ins welcome, though signature dishes run higher than a casual budget.

Fails 2-source 'high'. — Prior note: The shop's entire curry concept is built around using no wheat flour and no sugar — the roux is thickened without flour and all curries are described as gluten-free. The official site and multiple write-ups state the curry is made 砂糖・小麦粉不使用 (no sugar, no wheat flour). This makes it one of the most gluten-aware spots in central Kanazawa. However, it is not a certified dedicated celiac kitchen; toppings, side items (pickles, soup) and cross-contamination handling are not explicitly documented, so highly sensitive celiacs should confirm specific items and shared-surface risk directly with staff.
kz_kanazawa_nanahoshi_curry.vegan_detail: Has clear vegan-friendly options rather than being a fully vegan restaurant (chicken and beef curries are on the regular menu). The 豆カレー (bean curry) is made for vegetarian, macrobiotic, vegan and Muslim diners and excludes the five pungent roots (五葷: garlic, scallions, rakkyo, nira, asatsuki). A newer vegan curry, カカオとナッツのごちそうカレー (cacao & nut curry), is dairy-free, gluten-free and plant-based using coconut milk, nuts and okara-konjac. Vegan diners should confirm which curries and toppings are plant-based on the day, as the menu rotates seasonally.
kz_kanazawa_nanahoshi_curry.hours_raw: Mon 11:00-14:00; Tue 11:00-15:00; Wed-Sat 11:00-19:00; Sun 11:00-16:00 (hours vary by day across sources; official site notes 11:00-19:30, closed Mondays). Lunch-focused; afternoon/evening availability varies.
kz_kanazawa_nanahoshi_curry.notes: An independent curry specialist in central Kanazawa. The result is a personal, ingredient-driven take on Kanazawa cu

chef_bio.background: An independent curry specialist in central Kanazawa. The owner spent more than 15 years researching curry, including time overseas (such as Canada), before realizing a long-held dream of opening the shop around 2015. The result is a personal, ingredient-driven take on Kanazawa curry.
chef_bio.philosophy: Food that is delicious and makes the body feel good — gently made, light on the stomach, and accessible to people of every dietary style. The shop frames itself as offering 'the most Kanazawa-like Kanazawa curry in the world' with a spirit of omotenashi (hospitality).
chef_bio.specialty: A refined Kanazawa-style curry made, by the shop's own description, with no sugar and no wheat flour and seasoned with 27 spices. The signature 金澤ななほしカレーセット lets diners choose two curries from options such as chicken, bean, and a seasonal curry, served with a nut-milk soup, original Japanese-style pickles, and a dessert of the day. Seasonal curries (e.g. pork with bamboo shoot and bitter melon, or squid in a squid-ink base) rotate through the year. The bean curry is built for vegetarian/vegan/macrobiotic/Muslim diners with the five pungent roots omitted, and a cacao-and-nut vegan curry has been added.

anecdotes.text: The owner researched curry for over 15 years, including overseas study such as in Canada, before opening the shop around 2015 to realize a long-held dream.
The bean curry is made so vegetarian, macrobiotic, vegan and Muslim diners can all eat it, omitting the five pungent vegetables (garlic, scallion, rakkyo, nira, asatsuki).
The shop describes its curry as containing no sugar and no wheat flour and using 27 spices, positioning itself as a body-friendly, healthy Kanazawa curry.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: corezo は砂糖・小麦粉不使用と27種のスパイス、五葷(ニンニク・ねぎ・らっきょう・にら・あさつき)抜きの豆カレー(ベジ/マクロビ/ビーガン/ムスリム対応)を確認。weekend-kanazawa は豆カレーの五葷抜きと新作カカオ&ナッツのビーガンカレーを裏付け。jinomon/hokuriku-curry は店主がカナダ等を含め15年以上カレーを研究し2015年に開業したことを裏付け(公式サイトは物語部分を明記せず)。アレルギー/GFは店の自称の紹介にとどめ安全性は断定しない。

staff_allergy_handling.text: The shop is explicitly oriented toward dietary needs, stating it wants to serve diners of every food style, with a dedicated five-pungent-free bean curry for vegetarian/vegan/macrobiotic/Muslim guests.

positives.text: All curries are made with no wheat flour and no sugar, making the core dishes inherently gluten-free rather than relying on a single modified menu item.
Offers a dairy-free, gluten-free, plant-based cacao-and-nut vegan curry alongside the five-pungent-free bean curry.
The curry is described as additive-free and oil-light (no-oil/ノンオイル, 無添加 in the shop's own positioning), aimed at being easy on the stomach.

cultural_comfort.note: A welcoming, health-focused curry shop used to explaining its gluten-free and vegetarian options; a few words of Japanese and pointing at the menu will get a foreign student a comfortable, no-reservation lunch.

gf_review.why: Legitimately skips wheat-flour roux (rice flour instead) — good — so GF options plausible. BUT base curry seasoned with soy sauce AND miso per their own page (standard shoyu=wheat, miso may be barley), unverified. No allergen menu, no tamari sourcing, no CC protocol. Zero independent celiac confirmation — every 'all GF' claim is own marketing. Fails 2-source 'high'.
red_flags: Soy sauce AND miso in the curry base, wheat/barley status unverified
Venue says wheat-allergic diners should double-check
'No wheat flour' scoped to chicken curry only
No independent celiac 'ate here and was fine' report
gf_review.plain_rice: Curry-over-plain-white-rice; rice is GF — the risk is the sauce, not the rice.

kz_wa_shokuba_hasuya_honten.gf_detail: No gluten-free program. This is a Kaga-cuisine seafood izakaya built around soy sauce, dashi, and fried/simmered dishes; jibuni is thickened with flour and seasoned with soy-based seasonings, and the menu relies heavily on wheat-containing soy sauce. No dedicated gluten-free menu, fryer, or allergen handling is documented. Not suitable for celiacs.
kz_wa_shokuba_hasuya_honten.vegan_detail: The restaurant is centered on fresh seafood from Kanazawa Port (nodoguro, sashimi) and Kaga dishes like duck jibuni; nearly everything involves fish, meat, or fish/bonito dashi. No vegan or vegetarian menu is documented. A vegetarian could perhaps ask about plain Kaga vegetable preparations, but dashi exposure is likely throughout.

chef_bio.background: Hasuya is a Kaga regional-cuisine seafood izakaya in the heart of Kanazawa's Katamachi/Kiguramachi nightlife district, just off Korinbo. The kitchen works on a local-production-for-local-consumption principle, building its menu around seasonal Kaga vegetables and fish landed at Kanazawa Port. The main branch is about a five-minute drive from Kanazawa Station.
chef_bio.philosophy: Local production for local consumption (地産地消): showcasing the seasonal vegetables and seafood of Ishikawa in dishes meant to be both beautiful to look at and delicious to eat, keeping to the fundamentals while leaving room for a playful touch.
chef_bio.specialty: Signature dishes include nodoguro (rich, fatty throat-fish) preparations, fresh sashimi platters from the daily Kanazawa Port catch, and Kaga lotus root cooked many ways. House favorites are hasu-mushi (steamed lotus root with a chewy texture and gentle flavor) and kamo no jibuni, the classic Kaga simmered-duck dish. The 'Kaga Umaichi Set' (around 2,980 yen) bundles nodoguro, a local simmered item, and steamed lotus root.

anecdotes.text: The shop's name plays on renkon (lotus root), which the kitchen treats as a signature ingredient across the menu.
There is a sister location, Hasuya Kanazawa Ekimae-ten, near Kanazawa Station, making the Katamachi shop the honten (main store).

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Official site (hasuya-honten.com) and the Kiguramachi district guide describe a lotus-root-themed Kaga washoku izakaya in Kigura-machi 1-10, with nodoguro courses, hasu-mushi, jibuni, and the Kaga Umaichi set; both stress 地産地消 and a Kanazawa Station branch.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Kaga cuisine such as jibuni is thickened with flour and seasoned with wheat-based soy sauce; no gluten-free handling is documented.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The menu is built on Japanese seasonings (soy sauce, dashi); standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat. No wheat-free soy sauce is mentioned.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Dishes rely on fish/bonito dashi and the kitchen centers on seafood and meat, so plant-only dishes would likely still contact animal-based dashi.

cultural_comfort.note: A lively local Kaga-cuisine izakaya where a few words of Japanese and pointing at dishes will go a long way; little English is documented, but staff accept cards and cashless payment so ordering is manageable.

kz_sabou_bar_gauche.gf_detail: Not a gluten-free destination and not celiac-safe. The food menu centers on house cheesecake, gateau chocolat, cake, and an original eggplant curry over saffron rice (curry roux/sauce typically contains wheat). There is no documented gluten-free menu, gluten-free preparation, or allergen handling. A celiac traveler should not assume any dish here is safe.
kz_sabou_bar_gauche.vegan_detail: Not a vegan or vegetarian destination. The signature sweets (cheesecake, gateau chocolat) contain dairy and eggs. The Gauche-style eggplant curry on saffron rice may be vegetable-forward but is not documented as vegan and could contain dairy/meat-based stock. Siphon coffee (Toraja blend) and herbal teas are available and can be enjoyed black/plant-based. Vegans would need to ask directly; no plant-based menu is documented.

chef_bio.origin: The name 'Gauche' (ゴーシュ) is widely understood to reference Kenji Miyazawa's story 'Gorsch the Cellist' (セロ弾きのゴーシュ), an association echoed by visitor reviews, though the sources reviewed do not have the shop state this explicitly.
chef_bio.background: Tucked into a quiet back lane of Kanazawa's historic Higashi Chaya geisha district (Higashiyama 1-16-5), Gauche occupies a charming old machiya (traditional wooden townhouse). Step off the bustling main avenue and the atmosphere shifts: a latticed-window facade keeps the interior hidden from passersby while those inside enjoy a soft view out. The space leads a double life, opening as a tranquil tea house from late morning (around 11:00) and transforming into an intimate adult bar after 19:00.
chef_bio.philosophy: An intentionally intimate, unhurried 'adult time' aesthetic. The owner curates the mood down to the music, with Edith Piaf on the sound system, encouraging guests to linger and slow down by the lattice window.
chef_bio.specialty: By day, siphon-brewed coffee is the star: made with a Toraja blend and brewed cup by cup, served with a refill pot for roughly three cups while you settle by the lattice window. Sweets include a house cheesecake and other house-made chocolate confections, and the kitchen's original 'Gauche-style eggplant curry' layers plenty of sliced eggplant over saffron rice scented with cumin. By night it becomes a connoisseur's bar with roughly 300 whiskies, 150 wines, 80 calvados and 25 sherries, plus calvados highballs and cigars.

anecdotes.text: Each cup of siphon coffee is brewed individually and comes with a refill pot for about three more cups, best enjoyed seated by the latticed window.
Unusually for the Higashi Chaya area, it stays open late into the night, with a bar selection of around 300 whiskies, 150 wines and 80 calvados.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: food-japon.com confirms the Higashi Chaya machiya, 11:00-19:00 tea house then bar, Toraja siphon coffee with a ~3-cup refill pot, Edith Piaf, the eggplant curry, and the 300 whiskies / 150 wines / 80 calvados / 25 sherries counts. The Miyazawa name link is a common association (Tripadvisor) not asserted by the shop in these sources.

positives.text: Siphon-brewed coffee (Toraja blend) and herbal teas are available and can be ordered plain, which are naturally suitable options for plant-based and gluten-avoiding guests.

cultural_comfort.note: A tiny, atmospheric machiya hidden on a back lane where the owner curates a quiet adult mood, so come relaxed and ready to communicate mostly in Japanese; daytime siphon coffee is the easiest entry point for a foreign student.
